apps.name: Helumi
apps.tagline: More space for your Mac, without buying a new one.
apps.description:
Helumi is a macOS application that adds a cloud drive to Finder with terabytes of space and zero bytes used on your Mac. Files look and open like normal, but they live in the cloud and stream only the parts you need, so large videos start playing instantly. This tool is designed for video editors, photographers, and creators who work with large files and are running out of disk space.

Key Features:

- Adds a Helumi drive in Finder, next to Macintosh HD, with up to 30 TB of space.

- Streams only the part of a file you need, so large videos start in under a second.

- Keeps files off your disk, with an option to keep folders offline.

- Shares files with a link and collects files from anyone.

- Restores deleted files for 30 days and resumes interrupted uploads.

Helumi is a macOS application that gives your Mac terabytes of cloud storage as a normal Finder drive, using zero local disk space. Files stream on demand, so even huge videos open instantly.

apps.name: MacWhisper
apps.tagline: Quickly transcribe audio files into text on your Mac
apps.description:
MacWhisper is a Mac transcription app that uses OpenAI's Whisper and Nvidia Parakeet to turn audio and video into accurate, searchable text in seconds. All transcription runs locally on your device with Metal and GPU acceleration.

Core features:
• Drag-and-drop transcription with up to 300x realtime speeds
• Records meetings, microphone, and system audio with automatic detection
• Speaker recognition, batch transcription, and YouTube video support
• Realtime captions with live translation, plus DeepL subtitle translation
• Integrates with ChatGPT, Claude, Groq, Ollama, and 100+ supported languages

Join thousands of journalists, researchers, students, and creators trusting MacWhisper for fast, private, on-device transcription.

apps.name: Anytype
apps.tagline: Local-first notes as typed objects, with encryption and peer-to-peer sync.
apps.description: Anytype is the notes app in the Logseq guide. It organizes information as typed objects with relations, keeps data local-first, and syncs peer-to-peer. The app has a free plan. Paid memberships add remote storage and sharing limits. Check current prices on anytype.io before you buy.

apps.name: iA Writer
apps.tagline: A focused markdown editor sold as a one-time purchase on the Mac.
apps.description: iA Writer is the writing app in the Ulysses guide. It is a markdown editor built around a calm page and plain-text files. The Mac app is a one-time purchase, sold separately from the iPhone, iPad, and Windows versions. The developer's buy page listed the Mac app at $49.99. Confirm the current price on ia.net before you buy.

apps.name: ClearBar
apps.tagline: Hides third-party menu bar icons and keeps them in one panel.
apps.description: ClearBar hides third-party menu bar icons and keeps those apps in one panel, where you can open a menu or quit the app. The developer says it needs macOS 26 or 27 on Apple silicon. The site listed a launch price of $5, then $12, as a one-time purchase. Check the price on the site before you buy.

apps.name: Lounge
apps.tagline: Hides menu bar icons and opens them from a notch panel.
apps.description: Lounge hides and reveals menu bar icons and opens a panel near the notch, with clipboard history in that panel. The developer says it needs macOS 26 or later. The site did not list a price when this was checked.

apps.name: Alcove
apps.tagline: A notch display for notifications and now playing.
apps.description: Alcove puts notifications, now playing, and status in a notch display styled like the iPhone Dynamic Island. The developer says it needs macOS 15 or later. The site did not list a price when this was checked. It is not a menu bar icon hider.

apps.name: HoldSpeak
apps.tagline: Dictation into any Mac app, on the device, paid once.
apps.description: HoldSpeak types what you say into the Mac app where the cursor is. The developer says transcription stays on the Mac, with no account, and that you pay once after a 7-day trial. It needs Apple silicon and macOS 14.6 or later. The site did not list a dollar price when this was checked.

apps.name: Precis
apps.tagline: On-device dictation that types where the cursor is.
apps.description: Precis types what you say into the app where the cursor is, and the developer says the audio stays on the Mac. The site listed a founding price of $19, then $29, paid once. It says the app needs macOS 26.5 on Apple silicon. Check the price before you buy.

apps.name: Voicera
apps.tagline: Dictation into any app, with a free weekly cap.
apps.description: Voicera types speech into the app you are using. The developer says audio is streamed for recognition and not kept after the text comes back. A free plan was listed at 500 words a week. Pro was listed at $12 a month, or $5 a month on the yearly plan. Check voicera.app before you subscribe.

apps.name: Shottr
apps.tagline: Screenshots, scrolling capture, OCR, and a screen ruler.
apps.description: Shottr takes screenshots, including scrolling captures, and adds OCR, a screen ruler, and a color picker. It runs on macOS 10.15 or later. The purchase page lists a one-time Basic license at $12, for one person and up to five computers, and says a free copy asks you to upgrade after 30 days. A license is required for commercial use. Check shottr.cc before you pay.

apps.name: Better Shot
apps.tagline: Free screenshots and screen recording, with annotation.
apps.description: Better Shot takes screenshots and records the screen, then lets you annotate or edit the video. The developer says it is free, with no account and no watermark, and that it needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. The site also calls it open source.

apps.name: DejaShot
apps.tagline: Search the screenshots you already took.
apps.description: DejaShot does not take the screenshot. It reads the text inside screenshots you already saved and notes which app they came from, so you can search them. The site listed a price of $4.99 and said it needs macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Screen Charm
apps.tagline: Records the screen, then zooms on each click.
apps.description: Screen Charm records the screen, camera, and audio, then applies a zoom on each click after the recording. The site listed a one-time price of $99, with $149 shown as the regular price, and said there is no subscription. macOS 14 or later is recommended.

apps.name: ScreenToast
apps.tagline: Demo recorder with click zooms and drafted narration.
apps.description: ScreenToast records a product demo and adds zooms on clicks. It can also draft a narration from what you did and read it aloud. The site listed Pro at $7 a month, or $59 a year, and said export needs Pro. It needs macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Boom
apps.tagline: Screen recording and live presentation, without a timeline.
apps.description: Boom records the screen and runs live presentations with layout changes and zoom, without an editing timeline. The site offers a free trial and did not list a price when this was checked. It needs macOS 13 or later.

apps.name: Tucket
apps.tagline: Clipboard history from the notch, kept on the Mac.
apps.description: Tucket keeps a history of what you copy and opens it from the MacBook notch. The developer says nothing you copy leaves the Mac. The site listed a lifetime price of $10, with $15 shown as the regular price, and said it needs macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Clippio
apps.tagline: On-device clipboard history, paid once.
apps.description: Clippio stores clipboard history on the Mac, with search, pins, and text recognition on copied images. The developer says there is no cloud sync. The site listed a one-time price of $6.90 and macOS 13 or later.

apps.name: Maclip
apps.tagline: Encrypted clipboard history on the Mac, paid once.
apps.description: Maclip stores clipboard history encrypted on the Mac, and it can paste several clips in order. The developer says clips are not uploaded, and that password-manager apps are ignored. The site listed $9.99 once for up to two Macs, with a 7-day trial, and macOS 13 or later.

apps.name: NotchDodo
apps.tagline: Music, timers, calendar, and files in the notch.
apps.description: NotchDodo turns the MacBook notch into a hover panel for music, timers, calendar, files, notes, and clipboard. The site listed a lifetime license at $9.99 and said it needs macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Droppy
apps.tagline: A Dynamic Island that also works without a notch.
apps.description: Droppy is a Dynamic Island for the Mac. On a Mac without a notch, or on an external display, it uses that island instead of a camera cutout. The site listed $9.99 once, with a three-day trial, and macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Mole
apps.tagline: Uninstall apps, map the disk, and clear caches.
apps.description: Mole uninstalls Mac apps together with leftover files, and it also maps disk usage and clears caches. The site listed $19 once, with a 14-day refund, and macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Plumby
apps.tagline: Finds leftover files and large caches you choose to remove.
apps.description: Plumby finds caches, old installers, iPhone backups, and files left behind after an app is dragged to the Trash. The site listed $29 a year or $79 once, and macOS 15 or later. It only removes what you select.

apps.name: Bytesweep
apps.tagline: Shows what is filling the disk, then deletes only what you approve.
apps.description: ByteSweep shows what is using disk space and cleans only what you approve. The developer says it does not remove anything until you say so, and that cleaned items can be restored for 7 days. The site listed $29.99 once, a 3-day Mac trial, and macOS 14 or later. It is a disk cleaner, not an app uninstaller.

apps.name: Peeka
apps.tagline: The eye break you'll look forward to.
apps.description:
Peeka is a tiny ghost for your Mac that reminds you to take 20-20-20 eye breaks. As your eyes tire, Peeka gets sleepy, covers your screen with a blanket and counts down while you look at something in the distance. Breaks can come every 20, 30, 45 or 60 minutes and last 20 seconds, 30 seconds or a minute, and you can pause for an hour or hide Peeka until break time. It waits for a pause in your typing, warns you a minute before a break and stays hidden during meetings, camera or mic use, screen shares, presentations and full-screen video. Peeka naps after five minutes of inactivity and restarts the timer when you return, you can skip with Esc or snooze for five minutes with no streaks to lose, and collectible items appear during breaks.

Key Features:

- 20-20-20 Breaks: gentle, customisable eye-rest reminders

- Adorable Ghost: Peeka gets sleepy and tucks in your screen

- Meeting Aware: hides during calls, screen shares and video

- Typing Aware: waits for pauses and warns before breaks

- Collectibles and No Guilt: rewards without streak pressure

Peeka makes healthy eye breaks something to look forward to, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time price of $19.

apps.name: Notchi
apps.tagline: Your personal AI, 100% in your control.
apps.description:
Notchi is a personal AI that was born in your Mac's notch and now goes beyond it. Type into the notch to ask a question with web search when needed, capture a note, set a reminder or run a coding agent on a project with your chosen folder and model. Everything happens in one continuous conversation with memory and history, and Notchi can run system commands to complete tasks and return rich answers including charts. Background tasks are tracked in the collapsed notch, long-press shortcuts and prompts work on selected text, and you get emoji reactions and suggested next questions. You bring your own model provider key, chats and memory are stored locally, and an Audit section in Settings lists every request sent, with no account, email or password required.

Key Features:

- Ask, Capture and Remind: AI answers, notes and reminders from the notch

- Code Mode: run a coding agent on any project

- Memory and History: one continuous conversation

- Background Tasks: tracked right in the collapsed notch

- Bring Your Own Key: local storage and a full request audit

Notchi puts a private, capable AI assistant in your Mac's notch, free and open source with your own model key.

apps.name: Satori
apps.tagline: A browser that gives you room to think.
apps.description:
Satori is a light, fast and quiet web browser for Mac built on WebKit, the engine behind Safari, with a download of about 6 MB. It preconnects to links you point at, suggests likely pages from your history in new tabs and puts idle tabs to sleep after half an hour unless they're kept awake or playing media. Spaces separate work and study with up to nine per window, and tab colours match each site's colour. Satori declines cookie banners for you, blocks ads and trackers, and strips tracking tags when you copy links. Focus mode, Reading mode and an Apple Intelligence summary help you concentrate, and nine ambient soundscapes plus binaural tones set the mood. You can turn web apps into Dock apps, import bookmarks and passwords from Chromium browsers and use Bitwarden, with no account, sync or telemetry.

Key Features:

- Lightweight WebKit Browser: about 6 MB and very fast

- Spaces and Tab Sleep: organised and efficient tabs

- Built-In Privacy: blocks ads, trackers and cookie banners

- Focus and Reading Modes: with AI summaries

- Ambient Soundscapes: nine sounds plus binaural tones

Satori is a calm, private and speedy browser for Apple silicon Macs, completely free.

apps.name: T-Scriptor
apps.tagline: You listen. Blot writes it down.
apps.description:
T-Scriptor is lecture and meeting transcription for Mac and iPhone that records and transcribes on your device, so your audio never leaves it. A live transcript with speaker labels follows along as you listen, and Blot, the app's friendly assistant, produces structured summaries of key concepts and upcoming work. Papers mentioned in class are linked to their page, DOI or a title search, with unlinked references listed under Also mentioned, and spoken deadlines and office hours become calendar events with the original quote attached. Tools to explain terms, replace transcripts and prepare for exams help you study, and encrypted two-way sync keeps your Mac and iPhone in step.

Key Features:

- On-Device Transcription: audio stays on your device

- Live Transcript: speaker labels in real time

- Smart Summaries: key concepts and upcoming work

- Citations and Calendar: papers linked, deadlines added automatically

- Study Tools: explain terms and exam prep

T-Scriptor makes lectures and meetings effortless to capture and review, free for 10 recordings a month with Plus at $9 a month or $89.99 a year.

apps.name: Taco Tuesday
apps.tagline: Dinner, sorted. Together.
apps.description:
Taco Tuesday is a shared household app for recipes, weekly meal plans and grocery lists. Clip recipes from links, social posts, pasted text or photos of handwritten cards, import collections from Paprika, Crouton or Mela, and save recipes straight from the iPhone share sheet. Everyone in the household can add recipes to a shared weekly meal plan and set servings, use Quick Add for meals without a recipe and subscribe to the plan in their calendar. The grocery list builds itself from planned meals, scales to servings, sorts by aisle, splits across stores and syncs check-offs across phones, and pantry items can be added by barcode or package photo. Cooking mode offers full-screen steps, timers, highlighted ingredients, hands-free voice control and Siri, along with ratings, cook history and reminders for favourites.

Key Features:

- Recipe Clipping: from links, social posts, text or handwritten cards

- Shared Meal Plan: the whole household plans together

- Smart Grocery List: scaled, sorted by aisle and synced

- Cooking Mode: full-screen steps, timers and voice control

- Ratings and Reminders: track favourites and cook history

Taco Tuesday takes the stress out of family dinners on iPhone, iPad and the web, with a 21-day free trial and then $2.99 a month or $29.99 a year for up to 5 people.

apps.name: Sight
apps.tagline: Look away. Your Mac blurs.
apps.description:
Sight blurs your Mac's screen the moment you look away, using the head tracking in AirPods Pro, AirPods Max or AirPods 3. The blur fades in within 0.18 seconds on every display, so nobody can read over your shoulder when you turn your head. You can set the trigger angle anywhere from 15 to 60 degrees in 5-degree steps, and each screen gets its own blur whether or not it's plugged in. One-click calibration and slow re-centering correct for sensor drift, and tracking stops automatically when the display sleeps or the session locks. Sight is a native Swift app with no dependencies that stays idle when not blurring, runs from the menu bar and processes everything locally.

Key Features:

- Instant Privacy Blur: screen blurs when you look away

- AirPods Head Tracking: works with AirPods Pro, Max and 3

- Adjustable Angle: trigger from 15° to 60°

- Every Display: separate blur on each screen

- Lightweight and Private: native, local and sleep-aware

Sight is a clever privacy shield for your Mac screen, with a free 24-hour trial and a price of €4.

apps.name: Blook
apps.tagline: Your bookmarks, without the clutter.
apps.description:
Blook is a private, lightweight bookmark manager for everyday links on macOS and Windows. It organises your bookmarks into boards and columns with a clean, distraction-free interface and drag-and-drop organisation. Global instant search opens with Command-K on Mac or Control-K on Windows, so any saved link is a keystroke away. Your bookmarks stay on your own device in a portable SQLite database that you can back up and sync through your existing cloud storage. There's zero tracking, no behavioural profiles and no ads.

Key Features:

- Boards and Columns: visual bookmark organisation

- Drag and Drop: rearrange links effortlessly

- Instant Search: Cmd+K to find any bookmark

- Portable Database: SQLite file you can back up and sync

- Private: no tracking, profiles or ads

Blook keeps your bookmarks tidy and private, free to download on the Mac App Store with a one-time purchase to unlock it fully.

apps.name: Tucklane
apps.tagline: Your notch, your way.
apps.description:
Tucklane is a small Mac utility that lives in the notch and opens when you hover over it, press Option-Space or click it. It shows artwork and playback controls for Spotify or Apple Music, and keeps your recent clipboard copies on your Mac. A file shelf lets you drop files on the notch to stash them, with files referenced rather than copied, and a scratchpad for notes saves automatically. A focus timer counts down right in the notch, and Tuck, an optional duckling mascot, reacts to your activity. On MacBooks with a notch it sits in the notch, and on other Macs it appears as a small pill at the top of the screen, with no account required.

Key Features:

- Music Controls: Spotify and Apple Music in the notch

- Clipboard History: recent copies kept locally

- File Shelf: drop files on the notch to stash them

- Notes and Focus Timer: quick scratchpad and countdowns

- Tuck the Duckling: an optional reactive mascot

Tucklane makes your Mac's notch handy and charming, free during beta and then a one-time $9.79 at launch.

apps.name: Gossip
apps.tagline: Mac and Android, finally on speaking terms.
apps.description:
Gossip links your Mac with Android phones and tablets, connecting directly over your local network or through an optional end-to-end encrypted relay when you're away, with no account required. It brings Universal Control from Mac to Android, screen mirroring with audio and Android apps as Mac windows, along with notification mirroring with inline replies. Clipboard sync covers text and images with a clipboard history, and Do Not Disturb and Focus stay in sync between devices. A media remote, Instant Hotspot, lock on leave, find my device, battery sync with low-battery alerts and SMS messages are included, and you can even use your phone as a trackpad and keyboard. Some advanced features require Shizuku on Android.

Key Features:

- Universal Control and Mirroring: control and view Android from your Mac

- Notification Mirroring: reply inline from the Mac

- Clipboard Sync: text, images and history across devices

- Continuity Extras: hotspot, find my device and battery alerts

- Private Connection: local network or encrypted relay, no account

Gossip brings Apple-style continuity to Mac and Android users, completely free and open source under Apache 2.0.

apps.name: Zipic
apps.tagline: Save space, keep quality.
apps.description:
Zipic is an image compression app for Mac and Windows that processes everything locally, so images are never uploaded and it works offline. Compress single files or whole batches by drag and drop, the Open button, the menu bar or the Finder right-click menu, choosing from six compression levels. You can resize images, convert between formats and save by replacing originals, adding a suffix or picking a location, and custom presets switch with one click. It supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF, GIF, PDF, SVG, APNG and ICNS. Pro adds Notch Drop, clipboard auto-compress, folder monitoring, metadata preservation and integrations with the zipic CLI, Apple Shortcuts, Raycast, a URL scheme and Finder quick actions.

Key Features:

- Batch Compression: drag, drop and shrink many images at once

- Six Compression Levels: balance size and quality

- Resize and Convert: change formats and dimensions

- Wide Format Support: JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF and more

- Pro Automation: folder monitoring, Shortcuts, Raycast and CLI

Zipic makes image compression fast and private, free for 25 compressions a day with a one-time Personal license from $29.99.

apps.name: MightyBench
apps.tagline: Every tool your Mac was missing.
apps.description:
MightyBench is a native Mac app with 49 private tools for video, audio, images, PDFs and on-device AI. Video tools cover screen recording with auto-zoom and captions, downloading, compressing, converting, trimming, resizing, cropping, speed changes, merging, muting, audio replacement, subtitle burn-in and GIF creation. Audio tools record, trim, clean up noise, extract and convert audio and turn text into speech, while image tools convert, compress, resize, rotate, remove backgrounds, strip metadata, upscale, watermark and make QR codes. Twelve PDF tools merge, split, reorganise, compress, sign, protect and OCR documents, and intelligence tools handle transcription, dictation, text extraction, summaries, translation and content-based file search. Batch renaming, duplicate finding and zip tools round it out, all processed locally with originals left untouched.

Key Features:

- 13 Video Tools: record, compress, convert, trim and more

- Audio Tools: record, clean, convert and text-to-speech

- Image Tools: convert, remove backgrounds, upscale and watermark

- 12 PDF Tools: merge, split, sign, protect and OCR

- On-Device AI: transcription, summaries, translation and search

MightyBench replaces a drawer full of utilities with one private app, for a one-time launch price of $19 (regularly $49.99).

apps.name: Otterdock
apps.tagline: Group apps in your Mac Dock and keep each project together.
apps.description:
Otterdock is a Dock organiser for macOS that bundles apps, files, folders and web links into workflow groups, so each project stays together. Open grouped items from the Dock or from desktop and Notification Center widgets in small, medium and large sizes. A visual group editor makes building groups simple with drag-and-drop editing and in-group sorting. Pro adds icon skins to tell groups apart, and the direct edition brings custom popups, click or hover access, global group shortcuts, keyboard navigation, Command-1 to 9 quick launch and per-file opening apps with previews. Groups and file paths are stored locally and optional analytics can be turned off.

Key Features:

- Workflow Groups: apps, files, folders and links together

- Dock and Widgets: open groups from the Dock or desktop

- Visual Editor: drag and drop to build and sort groups

- Pro Skins and Shortcuts: icon skins, hotkeys and quick launch

- Local Storage: no account, optional analytics

Otterdock keeps your Mac Dock tidy and project-focused, free for 2 groups with a one-time Pro upgrade of $6.99.

apps.name: Scrubs
apps.tagline: See what fills your Mac. Clear it out safely.
apps.description:
Scrubs is a disk space analyzer for Mac that maps your whole drive, sizing each folder by the space it actually uses and colouring it by kind. You can search by name or extension and rescan anytime, and switch between Map and Outline, Largest Files, Cleanup suggestions and Unused Apps views. Storage is broken down into Developer, Media, Apps, Documents, System and Other, and you can scan as administrator to see other users' files. A menu bar display shows free space for each drive with an alert below 10% free. Scrubs deletes only the items you select, moving them to the Trash first with undo, and shows how much space a permanent delete will free before it happens.

Key Features:

- Drive Map: see every folder sized and colour-coded

- Largest Files and Unused Apps: find space hogs fast

- Cleanup Suggestions: safe items to clear

- Menu Bar Monitor: free space and low-disk alerts

- Safe Deletes: Trash first with undo

Scrubs makes it easy to see and reclaim disk space on Apple silicon Macs, free for scanning with a one-time license of $14.99 (launch price $9.99).

apps.name: Helix
apps.tagline: A weapon wheel for your Mac.
apps.description:
Helix is a radial menu for Mac inspired by game weapon wheels. Hold Option-Space or a mouse button you choose to open a ring of tools around your pointer, then point at a tool and let go, or tap to keep the ring open and click or press a number. It packs 16 tools in two rings of eight, including clipboard history, screenshots, notes, a calculator, to-dos, volume, links and apps. Ask AI opens a chat panel for Claude or GPT with your own API key, and a clock offers timers, a stopwatch, pomodoro and alarms. Unit and currency conversion, window snapping, Reminders synced to iPhone, voice memos, screen recording and a colour picker are also included, with Spotify or Apple Music controls in the centre of the ring and three visual styles that follow light and dark mode.

Key Features:

- Radial Menu: hold ⌥Space, point and release

- 16 Built-In Tools: clipboard, screenshots, notes, calculator and more

- Ask AI: Claude or GPT chat with your own key

- Timers and Conversions: pomodoro, alarms, units and currency

- Music and Styles: playback controls and three looks

Helix puts your everyday tools one flick away on the Mac, for an early-bird one-time price of $4.99 (regularly $9.99).

apps.name: Citenook
apps.tagline: The private ChatGPT that lives on your Mac.
apps.description:
Citenook is a private AI assistant for Mac that answers general questions, helps you write and finds answers in your own files, showing the exact sentence behind each answer. Press Option-Space in any app for Quick Ask or writing tools that rewrite, shorten or fix your text. File answers come with numbered sources that open the exact passage, and you can keep separate brains for each client or project with folder sync. It reads PDFs including scans, Word documents, spreadsheets, text, recordings, Apple Notes, Obsidian, web pages, YouTube and Notion. Personal details are hidden before any online AI request, with a preview of what gets sent, and it can work fully offline with a model on your Mac or with your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or OpenRouter keys. Pro adds Ollama and LM Studio, deep answers, workflows and a learned writing style.

Key Features:

- Cited Answers: every answer links to the exact source passage

- Quick Ask Anywhere: Option-Space for questions and writing help

- Project Brains: separate knowledge bases per client or project

- Wide File Support: PDFs, Word, Notes, Obsidian, YouTube and more

- Private by Design: hides personal data, works offline or with your keys

Citenook is a private, source-backed AI assistant for your Mac, with a 30-day free trial and plans from $79 a year.

apps.name: Textlore
apps.tagline: Everything your friends told you to try, found in your texts.
apps.description:
Textlore is a Mac app that reads your iMessage and WhatsApp for Mac history to surface what matters, without ever sending, editing or deleting messages, and nothing leaves your Mac. Recs lists the books, shows, places, songs and apps friends recommended, with who said it, when and their exact words, sorted by how many people recommended each one. Promises lists the things you said you'd do, how many days late each is and which are still open, with reminders and a jump to Messages. Instant search covers every year with filters for sender, date and photos, and Option-Space opens quick search from any app. An archive saves every message and photo as it arrives, exports go to PDF, HTML, text, Markdown, CSV or image with contact details hidden, and Your Lore shows yearly stats as tree-ring visuals. Ask AI answers questions about your texts with the source messages.

Key Features:

- Recs: every recommendation friends gave you, ranked

- Promises: track what you said you'd do

- Instant Search: all years with sender, date and photo filters

- Archive and Export: save every message and export in many formats

- Ask AI and Your Lore: answers with sources and yearly stats

Textlore turns years of texts into something useful and private, free for 14 days and then a one-time price from $20 covering 2 Macs.

apps.name: Deskwatch
apps.tagline: Walk away from your MacBook.
apps.description:
Deskwatch is a menu bar theft alarm for MacBooks that uses the motion sensor already inside your Mac. Once armed, if someone lifts or shoves your MacBook, it sounds a siren at maximum volume, ignoring your volume setting, and locks the screen, and only Touch ID or your password can stop it. Closing the lid also triggers the alarm while protection is on, and a short countdown gives you time to disarm if you pick up the Mac yourself. It's smart enough to ignore typing, table knocks and dropped objects. You can arm it with one click or automatically when you lock your Mac, and disarming, quitting or changing settings all require Touch ID or a password. It can run a Shortcut when the alarm fires, keeps the Mac awake while protecting it, and works with no account, cloud or tracking.

Key Features:

- Motion Alarm: siren at full volume when the Mac is moved

- Auto Screen Lock: locks instantly when the alarm fires

- Lid-Close Trigger: alarm sounds if the lid is shut

- Smart Detection: ignores typing, knocks and dropped objects

- Touch ID Protected: needed to disarm, quit or change settings

Deskwatch lets you step away from your MacBook with peace of mind, for a one-time price of $4.99 on Apple silicon MacBooks.

apps.name: Up A Notch
apps.tagline: Know what needs your response.
apps.description:
Up A Notch shows your selected commitments in a single, low-noise view near your MacBook's notch so you always know what needs your response. With opt-in local Claude Code activity, it shows recent work, pending requests and completed turns, and lets you Allow or Deny Claude Code requests right from the notch or resume sessions in your terminal. It also detects Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Aider and Ollama as running processes. Selected Google Calendar events appear with a join action, and pre-call alerts warn you when agents are waiting on your input. Local todos and a focus timer are built in, along with optional GitHub CLI and MCP health signals. A closed-notch summary shows one number per side, a recording mode shows only a red dot while OBS, Screen Studio, Loom or Riverside runs, and one button removes every change it makes.

Key Features:

- Agent Activity: Claude Code requests, turns and sessions in the notch

- Allow or Deny: approve Claude Code requests without switching apps

- Calendar and Pre-Call Alerts: join meetings and see waiting agents

- Todos and Focus Timer: local tasks right by the notch

- Recording Mode and Clean Removal: privacy while streaming, one-click uninstall

Up A Notch keeps your agents, meetings and todos in one calm notch view, currently free in an invite-only private beta.

apps.name: Rekey
apps.tagline: Never type in the wrong language again.
apps.description:
Rekey is a keyboard layout fixer for Mac that detects text typed in the wrong keyboard layout and corrects it in under 200 milliseconds. It spots wrong-layout words as you type, starting from the very first word, and rewrites whole phrases, waiting for more context when a single letter is ambiguous. Using language statistics and dictionaries, it distinguishes between 34 languages, and corrections apply about 200 ms after you press Space, with adjusted timing for Slack and Discord. Press Command-Z within 5 seconds to undo a correction, after which Rekey leaves that word alone, and exceptions let you pin words that should never switch or assign words to a specific language. It skips password fields, terminals and code editors, and processes your typing entirely on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Automatic Layout Fixing: corrects wrong-layout typing instantly

- 34 Languages: detected with statistics and dictionaries

- Phrase-Aware: waits for context on ambiguous letters

- Quick Undo and Exceptions: Cmd+Z and custom word rules

- Safe and Private: skips passwords and code, processes locally

Rekey ends the frustration of typing in the wrong keyboard layout on your Mac, completely free.

apps.name: Ribbon for Mac
apps.tagline: Your Mac, in one long row.
apps.description:
Ribbon is a scrolling window manager for macOS that places your windows side by side on a strip wider than the screen, so opening new apps never shrinks the windows you already have. You scroll to reach them, sliding the strip with Option-scroll or a three-finger swipe. A clickable strip bar shows an icon for each column, with click-to-jump and drag-to-reorder, and you can stack windows or fold columns into tabs. Every display and every Space gets its own strip, layouts can be saved and restored at login, and dialogs and fixed-size windows float automatically along with any apps you choose. An optional focus border and dimming highlight the active window, a setup checker flags conflicting macOS settings and window managers, and a ribbon:// URL scheme and command-line tool support automation.

Key Features:

- Endless Strip: windows side by side, never shrunk

- Strip Bar: click to jump and drag to reorder columns

- Stacks and Tabs: group windows within a column

- Per-Display Strips and Saved Layouts: restore setups at login

- Automation: ribbon:// links and a command-line tool

Ribbon gives your Mac a smooth scrolling window workflow, for a one-time price of $9.99 for one Apple silicon Mac.

apps.name: Rollcage
apps.tagline: AI agents break things. Rollcage puts them back.
apps.description:
Rollcage is a macOS menu bar app that protects your projects from AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor. It snapshots your project when an agent starts and every 15 minutes after, using APFS clones that take under a second and little extra space. Session undo reports every file an agent deleted, edited or created and every command it ran, and one click restores the session while keeping your later edits. A mass-delete alarm warns when many files disappear quickly, and Guard blocks access to secret files, destructive commands and commits that contain keys or .env files, pausing risky actions like pushes to main for your approval. A network guard blocks paste and tunnel sites, and extras include agent alerts, Claude and Codex limit tracking, a secrets leak scan, token and cost tracking and a free MCP server.

Key Features:

- Automatic Snapshots: instant APFS clones of your project

- Session Undo: see and reverse everything an agent did

- Mass-Delete Alarm: alerts when files vanish quickly

- Guard: blocks secrets access and destructive commands

- Network Guard and Alerts: limit sites and track usage

Rollcage is a safety net for coding with AI agents, priced at $10 once per Mac with all future updates.

apps.name: Tilemode
apps.tagline: The keyboard cockpit for your Mac.
apps.description:
Tilemode is a keyboard cockpit for your Mac where every site is an app, every app has a key and every window is a tile. Turn any website into a standalone Mac app with its own window, icon, Dock spot, Command-Tab entry and separate login. Global hotkeys launch, focus, cycle or hide any app, including native ones, with an optional leader-key mode and warnings for conflicting shortcuts. Keyboard tiling snaps windows to halves, thirds, quarters, main-plus-stack or full-screen fill, with arrow keys to move focus and Shift to move windows. Per-app tiling rules and named layouts can be recalled with one key, tiles respect the menu bar and notch on every display, and all settings live in one readable config file that coding agents can manage through its command-line tool.

Key Features:

- Website Apps: turn any site into a standalone Mac app

- Global Hotkeys: one key to launch or focus any app

- Keyboard Tiling: halves, thirds, quarters and stacks

- Layouts and Rules: save and recall window setups

- Plain-Text Config: one readable file, agent friendly

Tilemode puts your apps and windows under complete keyboard control, with a founding one-time price of $9 for one Mac (then $29).

apps.name: Disklumo
apps.tagline: Make room on your Mac.
apps.description:
Disklumo is an all-in-one Mac cleaner that shows every file before anything moves and sends cleaned files to the Trash by default. Clean finds app and developer caches, AI tool files, logs, leftovers from uninstalled apps, System Data and package manager caches. Apps uninstalls programs with their related files, lists available updates and manages login items and background services. Analyze shows a disk map, your largest files, file search, growth since the last scan and external drives, while Status displays a health score with live CPU, GPU, memory, battery, network and fan readings. Optimize runs 17 maintenance tasks, a duplicates and old files tool finds byte-identical copies, old iPhone backups and installers, and extra tools include Stay Awake, Wipe Mode, fan and battery control and a free clipboard history.

Key Features:

- Clean: caches, logs, leftovers and System Data

- Apps: uninstall, updates and login items

- Analyze: disk map, largest files and growth tracking

- Status and Optimize: live health stats and 17 maintenance tasks

- Duplicates and Tools: old files, Stay Awake and fan control

Disklumo brings eight careful cleaning and system tools together for a one-time price of $17 on Apple silicon Macs.

apps.name: CopyPasta
apps.tagline: Your clipboard, served from the notch.
apps.description:
CopyPasta is a macOS clipboard manager that opens from the notch, or a virtual notch on Macs without one, when you hover over it or press Control-Command-C. It saves text, links, code, JSON, images, screenshots, files, vector graphics and colours, and merges identical repeat copies into one entry. Passwords, API keys and tokens are hidden, and older clips require Touch ID or your Mac password to view. Paste Stack pastes copied items one by one in order, and full-history search comes with category tabs and keyboard controls. It reads text from screenshots, includes an image editor with blur and a beautifier with social media presets, and shows colour cards with HEX, RGB and HSL values. Data is encrypted with AES-256, with optional iCloud sync.

Key Features:

- Notch Clipboard: hover the notch or press ⌃⌘C

- Everything Saved: text, code, images, files and colours

- Secure by Default: hides secrets, Touch ID for older clips

- Paste Stack: paste multiple items in order

- Screenshot Tools: OCR, blur editor and beautifier

CopyPasta makes your clipboard history beautiful and secure from the notch, with a 7-day free trial and one-time launch prices from $14.99.

apps.name: Afterword
apps.tagline: Meeting notes on your Mac. Private, no bot in the call.
apps.description:
Afterword is a meeting notes app for Mac that writes your notes for you without an account or a bot joining the call. It starts recording automatically when a Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams call begins and transcribes everything on your Mac, so audio and text never leave the machine. Each call is saved as a Markdown file with a summary, decisions, action items and the full transcript, in a folder you choose. It lives in the menu bar with a visible recording indicator and plays a calm one-minute sound when the call ends. A speech-tuned mode removes ums and repeats and learns custom names and words, it can translate between your language and theirs during the call, and it can rewrite broken English into clear sentences while keeping the word-for-word transcript.

Key Features:

- Auto Recording: starts when Zoom, Meet or Teams calls begin

- On-Device Transcription: audio and text stay on your Mac

- Markdown Notes: summary, decisions, action items and transcript

- Live Translation: both languages saved

- Clean Rewrites: removes fillers and polishes English

Afterword gives you private, automatic meeting notes on your Mac, with a 7-day free trial and then $29 a year or $39 for a lifetime license.

apps.name: Sequence Tool
apps.tagline: Transcript-led video editing.
apps.description:
Sequence Tool is a native Mac app for shaping podcasts and interviews from a transcript. Recordings are transcribed on your device, and you edit the story by hiding or restoring words, reordering sentences and clips and marking story beats, with every change reversible. It reviews filler words, silences, profanity and suggested retakes, and normalises audio for social, podcast or broadcast delivery. Variants let you create multiple cuts from one recording, such as a full episode, a clean version, chapters and social clips, each with its own edits and framing. Optional speaker detection and naming, multi-cam syncing with picture-in-picture and split-screen layouts, and shareable Sequence Packages are included, and you can export video or audio or hand off to Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Key Features:

- Transcript Editing: cut and reorder video by editing text

- On-Device Transcription: no media uploaded

- Clean-Up Review: fillers, silences and retakes

- Variants: full episodes, chapters and social clips from one recording

- Multi-Cam and Export: sync cameras and hand off to Final Cut or Resolve

Sequence Tool makes editing spoken video as easy as editing a document, with a seven-day free trial before a paid plan.

apps.name: Encore Display
apps.tagline: Turn your old iMac into a monitor.
apps.description:
Encore is Mac software that lets an old Intel iMac serve as an external display for another Mac over a single cable, with no hardware changes. It drives the iMac at up to 5K resolution and 60 fps for smooth windows and video, and you can arrange, mirror or set it as the main display in System Settings. It's plug-and-play: the picture appears in about two seconds, and unplugging returns your windows to the main Mac. The iMac's speakers and microphone work too, controlled with the volume keys, brightness follows your MacBook, Night Shift applies to both screens and sleep and wake stay in sync. It even works with your MacBook lid closed while on power, and supports Intel iMacs from late 2012 onward over Thunderbolt, USB-C or Ethernet.

Key Features:

- iMac as Monitor: reuse an old iMac as a second screen

- Up to 5K at 60 fps: sharp, smooth display output

- Plug and Play: picture appears in about two seconds

- Speakers and Mic: use the iMac's audio with volume keys

- Synced Brightness and Sleep: works as one setup

Encore gives your old iMac a second life as a beautiful display, free for 72 hours and then a one-time $49 purchase.

apps.name: Penfont
apps.tagline: Your handwriting, as a real font.
apps.description:
Penfont turns your handwriting into a real font you can type with in Pages, Keynote, TextEdit, Figma and anywhere else on your Mac. Print the template, write each letter in its box and take a photo, and Penfont finds every letter, lines them up and builds a working font in seconds. You can also start from pages you've already written, like notebook pages and letters, in a beta mode that reads the words itself. Fix any letter by moving, resizing, cleaning up or redrawing it, and letter variants keep repeated letters from looking stamped. Add Light and Bold weights from the same handwriting, then install the font with one click or export .ttf and .woff files to share. Everything happens on your Mac with no uploads or accounts.

Key Features:

- Photo to Font: template or existing notebook pages

- Letter Editing: move, resize, clean up or redraw

- Natural Variants: repeated letters look hand-written

- Light and Bold Weights: from the same handwriting

- One-Click Install: or export .ttf and .woff files

Penfont makes a personal handwriting font effortless and private, available on the Mac App Store for $12.99.

apps.name: Lunille
apps.tagline: Your Mac's notch, brought to life.
apps.description:
Lunille turns the notch on your Mac into a living island for music, accessories, calendar, Focus and coding assistants. Now Playing shows album art and a beat display for Music, Spotify and browser audio, and new tracks slide out with their cover. Your AirPods, headphones, keyboards, mice and controllers appear as 3D models in their real colours with battery rings, and charging and Low Power Mode states are shown too. You can start timers from the menu, a shortcut or a script, see when Do Not Disturb turns on, get meeting reminders with Join buttons for Zoom, Meet, Teams and FaceTime, and know when coding assistants finish or need you. Notifications, a file tray for AirDrop, Keep Awake, weather and custom volume and brightness indicators are included, along with Luni, an optional animated moon companion.

Key Features:

- Now Playing: album art and beat display for any player

- 3D Accessories: AirPods and devices with battery rings

- Calendar and Focus: meeting Join buttons and DND status

- Coding Assistant Alerts: know when agents finish

- Luni and Extras: animated companion, file tray and Keep Awake

Lunille makes the Mac notch delightful and useful, free for 14 days and then a one-time $9.99 at launch.

apps.name: Shepi
apps.tagline: Herdr's agents, a pleasure to use.
apps.description:
Shepi is a native Mac client for Herdr, the terminal runtime that keeps your coding agents alive. It shows all your Herdr spaces, tabs and agents, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Copilot CLI, in real terminals on your Mac and remote servers. Each agent shows its status in the sidebar, and the one that needs you turns amber, with banners, macOS notifications and an inbox for anything you missed. Agents can ask questions with buttons, open web pages and report progress, and their changes appear as side-by-side or unified diffs. You can add machines over SSH to one sidebar, split, zoom and drag panes between tabs, search across every space, agent and machine, and automate keystrokes with macros.

Key Features:

- Native Herdr Client: all agents in real terminals

- Needs-You Alerts: amber status, banners and an inbox

- Interactive Agents: buttons, web pages and progress

- Readable Diffs: side-by-side or unified changes

- Multi-Machine: SSH servers, global search and macros

Shepi turns Herdr's terminal agents into a polished Mac experience, with a 14-day free trial and a one-time price of $19.99.

apps.name: Current
apps.tagline: A MacUpdater alternative built for safer updates.
apps.description:
Current checks your Mac apps and command-line tools, verifies each update and installs it in one click. It lists Mac apps alongside Homebrew and npm global tools, and gets updates from each app's own source, whether Homebrew, Sparkle, Electron feeds or the App Store, so there's no database to go stale. Every update passes four checks before installing: the same developer as your current version, Apple notarization with checksum or signature matching, compatibility with your macOS version and chip, and a newer version number. The old version is kept until the new one passes its final check and restored if the install fails. Daily checks send notifications with an Update All button, open apps are quit normally so you can save and then reopened, and a current command-line tool and five colour themes are included.

Key Features:

- Apps and CLI Tools: Mac apps, Homebrew and npm in one list

- Four Safety Checks: developer, notarization, compatibility and version

- Automatic Rollback: restores the old version if an install fails

- Native Update Sources: Homebrew, Sparkle, Electron and App Store

- Daily Checks: notifications and one-click Update All

Current makes updating your Mac safe and effortless, priced at $3 one-time for the first 100 licenses and then $7.99.

apps.name: LocalEditor
apps.tagline: A local workspace for notes, sketches and code.
apps.description:
LocalEditor is a Mac workspace for reviewing and refining your AI agents' work in the folders already on your Mac. It opens existing folders or single files without importing or moving them, and offers Markdown editing with slash commands, wikilinks and nested subpages, a sandboxed live HTML preview and editable views for YAML, JSON, .env and .gitignore files. Images, video, PDFs and CSVs preview inline and code gets syntax highlighting. A canvas lets you draw shapes, connected arrows and freehand sketches and export to PNG, JPEG, SVG or PDF, and Command-1 and Command-2 open a quick note or blank canvas. Command-K searches across folders, files autosave and refresh live when they change on disk, and an MCP connection gives agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor scoped access with secret files blocked.

Key Features:

- Open Local Folders: no import, files stay where they are

- Markdown Editor: slash commands, wikilinks and subpages

- Live Previews: HTML, images, video, PDFs and CSVs

- Sketch Canvas: shapes, arrows and freehand drawing

- Agent Friendly: MCP access and conflict review

LocalEditor is a calm local home for notes, sketches and agent output, with a 14-day free trial and a one-time $20 purchase.

apps.name: Deskworthy
apps.tagline: Apps worth a place on your desk.
apps.description:
Deskworthy is a suite of careful, private Mac apps for disk space, cleanup, screenshots, images and system health. DiskAtlas shows where your disk space went and helps you recover it safely, and Kempt handles Mac maintenance by flagging safe-to-clear files, idle project clutter and what apps cost. Snipkeep captures screenshots with markup and a clickable history, Squish batch-compresses images to fit size limits while leaving originals untouched, and Telltale monitors your Mac and its apps live and over 30 days. VeilShot hides sensitive details in screenshots before you share them, and CopyHold is a clipboard manager with searchable history and collections, with a password manager called Lockwell coming soon.

Key Features:

- DiskAtlas and Kempt: find space and maintain your Mac

- Snipkeep: screenshots with markup and history

- Squish: batch image compression

- Telltale: system monitor over 30 days

- VeilShot and CopyHold: redact screenshots and manage clipboard

Deskworthy offers a growing family of focused Mac utilities at $5 each, or all apps for a $25 founder price, with 7-day trials.

apps.name: MACEQ
apps.tagline: Shape your sound.
apps.description:
MACEQ brings per-app EQ, volume and audio routing to your Mac. Each app gets its own 10-band equaliser from 31 Hz to 16 kHz with up to ±24 dB per band, plus its own volume from -48 dB to +6 dB. You can route each app to a different output, like speakers for music and headphones for calls, and routes, curves and levels are kept when apps relaunch. A single-knob compressor catches peaks, built-in and custom presets make tuning quick, and an all-audio mode applies one EQ, compressor and volume to everything. It needs no driver or kernel extension, adds only about 10 ms of latency and lives in the menu bar at around 0.5 MB. MACEQ Pro adds room correction that measures your speakers with a microphone and applies up to 10 filters.

Key Features:

- Per-App 10-Band EQ: tune each app separately

- Per-App Volume: from -48 dB to +6 dB

- Output Routing: send apps to different devices

- Compressor and Presets: tame peaks and save curves

- Pro Room Correction: measure and fix your speakers

MACEQ gives you studio-style control over every app's sound, for $9 one-time or $19 for Pro on Apple silicon Macs.

apps.name: Herdbell
apps.tagline: Watch every agent. Never leave your flow.
apps.description:
Herdbell is a macOS menu bar app that monitors Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor and Google Antigravity from a popup at your cursor. A session list shows each agent, project, status and elapsed time, and your pointer glows when an agent needs you, with optional sound and notifications. You can allow or deny commands, with risky ones requiring a second confirmation, and send quick replies or custom messages. An activity log records each session's commands, edits and errors, and agents connect in one click through their hooks with a backup saved first. Context Bridge builds a local handoff summary for another agent without calling an AI model, and everything stays on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Agent Dashboard: every session, status and elapsed time

- Pointer Glow Alerts: know when an agent needs you

- Allow or Deny: approve commands with safe double-checks

- Quick Replies and Activity Log: respond and review

- Context Bridge: hand off work between agents locally

Herdbell keeps all your AI agents in view without breaking focus, with a launch price of $9.99 (regularly $24.99) one-time.

apps.name: Nori
apps.tagline: The Git client beside your agents.
apps.description:
Nori is a light Git client for Mac, Windows and Linux that runs beside your IDE and AI agents. Its commit graph gives each branch a distinct colour, and you can drag and drop to merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or push. An interactive rebase planner lets you reorder, reword, squash, fixup or drop commits, and undo works for commits, branch deletions, stash drops and discards. Stage by hunk, line or selection, generate commit messages with your installed agent CLI, and resolve conflicts side by side with optional AI suggestions. Commit search filters by author, path, content, regex, date and hash, and a worktree view shows each agent's changes. Pro adds pushing and opening pull or merge requests on GitHub or GitLab, merge blockers, CI logs and issues.

Key Features:

- Colourful Commit Graph: drag and drop merges and rebases

- Interactive Rebase Planner: reorder, squash and reword

- Undo Everything: commits, branches and stashes

- Agent Friendly: AI commit messages and worktree view

- Pro PRs and Issues: GitHub and GitLab integration

Nori is a modern, agent-aware Git client, free for every Git feature with Pro at $20 once.

apps.name: Speakmac
apps.tagline: Type with your voice. In any Mac app.
apps.description:
Speakmac offers private dictation and bot-free meeting transcripts on your Mac. Type by speaking in any app with a cursor, including Gmail, Google Docs, Slack, Notes, ChatGPT and Claude, by holding a shortcut or using Hands Free mode. Writing styles for Default, Message and Email turn rough speech into polished text, and custom names and terms are corrected automatically. A searchable transcript history lets you edit, copy or replay audio, and you can drop in audio files to transcribe them. Meeting Mode records your microphone and meeting audio without a bot for Meet, Zoom, Teams, Slack, Discord, Webex, WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal. It supports 25 languages by default with optional local packs, and processing happens on your Mac with no account or API key.

Key Features:

- Dictate Anywhere: any app with a cursor

- Writing Styles: Default, Message and Email modes

- Transcript History: search, edit and replay audio

- Meeting Mode: bot-free recordings for major call apps

- Private and Multilingual: on-device, 25 languages

Speakmac is a private voice keyboard and meeting recorder for the Mac, free to try with a one-time license from $29 (₹699 in India).

apps.name: WidgetScreen
apps.tagline: Mac lock screen widgets.
apps.description:
WidgetScreen puts live weather, music, lyrics, photos and more right on your Mac's lock screen. It offers 28 widgets in sizes from Mini to Ultra Wide, including Weather, Calendar, Now Playing, Photos, Earth, Countdown, Agent Status, Audio Visualiser, Day Bar, Reminders and System. Widgets appear when your Mac locks and disappear when you sign in, and you arrange them by dragging onto a live preview, with changes saved automatically. Premium adds eight more widgets like Stock Ticker, Live Lyrics, Sticky Note, News, Devices and Daily Brief, plus extra clock faces, wider sizes, photo slideshows, tints and themes, ambient motion, saved layouts and smart display rules.

Key Features:

- 28 Lock Screen Widgets: weather, music, calendar, photos and more

- Live Preview Editor: drag, resize and save automatically

- Audio Visualiser: optional live audio effects

- Premium Widgets: lyrics, stocks, news and sticky notes

- Themes and Layouts: clock faces, tints and smart rules

WidgetScreen makes your Mac's lock screen useful and beautiful, free for the core widgets with Premium as a one-time purchase.

apps.name: Ribbon
apps.tagline: Every window. One ribbon.
apps.description:
Ribbon is a scrolling window manager for Mac that places each window in its own full-height column on a strip that extends past the edges of your screen, so windows never overlap or shrink. Move along the strip with a three-finger swipe or Control-Option and the arrow keys, and cycle window widths between one third, one half and two thirds or toggle full width. A strip map in six visual styles shows every window, with Control-Option-1 to 9 to jump and clickable tiles. Dialogs, picture-in-picture and fixed-size windows float, with per-app rules, and you can drag to resize or reorder. Each display gets its own strip, windows are restored when you quit, focus-follows-mouse is optional, and Ribbon can be scripted with ribbon:// links, a command-line tool and Raycast.

Key Features:

- Scrolling Strip: every window in its own full-height column

- Swipe Navigation: three-finger swipe or arrow keys

- Width Presets: one third, half, two thirds or full

- Strip Map: six styles with jump shortcuts

- Scriptable: ribbon:// links, CLI and Raycast

Ribbon brings an elegant scrolling workflow to Mac windows, for $15 once with a 7-day free trial and use on up to 3 Macs.

apps.name: SoundBuddy
apps.tagline: Pick your mic. It stays picked.
apps.description:
SoundBuddy is a small Mac companion for everyday audio that keeps your chosen microphone selected. With Input Lock, the mic you pick stays the default input while SoundBuddy is open, and if it disconnects, your chosen fallback takes over automatically. You can choose between your Mac's built-in microphone and a connected headset, and a quiet popup appears when a device connects, with battery shown when the device reports it. SoundBuddy also adds satisfying keyboard sounds with six packs, Blue Click, Brown Tactile, Red Linear, Thock, Creamy and Typewriter, each with volume control and off until you switch them on. Device controls and preferences stay on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Input Lock: your chosen mic stays selected

- Smart Fallback: switches to a backup mic if one disconnects

- Device Popup: quiet alerts when audio devices connect

- Keyboard Sounds: six mechanical and typewriter sound packs

- Local Controls: preferences stay on your Mac

SoundBuddy ends microphone mix-ups on the Mac, for a one-time launch price of $5 (then $9) with a seven-day refund.

apps.name: Moody
apps.tagline: Your home for visual inspiration.
apps.description:
Moody is a native macOS library for design inspiration that keeps everything on your Mac with no account or cloud required. Save screenshots, dragged-in files or pasted links, and link saves from X, Pinterest and LinkedIn keep the post and its images. On-device AI describes each save, reads the text in images and suggests tags, so you can search by visual content, on-image text and tags. Collections let you group saves by project or style, with one save allowed in many collections, and an inbox reviews iPhone screenshots synced to Photos. It supports images, GIFs, MP4 and MOV, offers a hidden section locked with Touch ID, bulk tagging and trashing, dragging saves out as original files, a 30-day trash and a local MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor.

Key Features:

- Save Anything: screenshots, files and links from X, Pinterest and LinkedIn

- On-Device AI: auto descriptions, text reading and tag suggestions

- Visual Search: find saves by content, text and tags

- Collections and Inbox: organise by project, review iPhone screenshots

- Private and Offline: local library with Touch ID hidden section

Moody is a calm, private home for every design reference you collect, currently free to use in beta.

apps.name: ToolKITZ
apps.tagline: The top drawer your Mac was missing.
apps.description:
ToolKITZ is a panel that drops down from the top of your Mac's screen holding a file shelf, clipboard history, notes, text capture and more than 70 modules, and hides when your cursor leaves. The File Shelf stores references so originals stay in place, letting you drag files in and out of apps. Clipboard history saves text, links, images and files with search, pinning and plain-text paste, and can skip password manager entries. Text Capture lets you draw a box over any on-screen text to copy it, and it also reads QR codes and barcodes. Modules include notes, to-dos, a focus timer, calendar and weather, and you can connect services like Stripe and GitHub with your own keys. Open it by scrolling at the top edge, hovering the notch, dragging a file up or pressing Control-Option-T, in Graphite, Glass or Black styles.

Key Features:

- Top Drawer Panel: drops down from the top edge or notch

- File Shelf: drag files in and out without moving originals

- Clipboard History: search, pin and plain-text paste

- Text Capture: copy on-screen text, QR codes and barcodes

- 71 Modules: notes, to-dos, focus, calendar, Stripe and GitHub

ToolKITZ gives your Mac a handy top drawer for everyday tools, free for the core features with Pro from $29.99 a year.

apps.name: RewriteBar
apps.tagline: Improve your writing, everywhere you write.
apps.description:
RewriteBar is an AI writing assistant for macOS that works in any app with a text field. Select text, press a keyboard shortcut and RewriteBar opens with your text and the available actions. It fixes grammar, spelling, tone and clarity, translates into more than 500 languages, and offers preset and custom AI actions plus a template library. You can compare the original and rewritten text line by line or word by word, and chain multiple actions into one flow. It integrates with PopClip, works with local AI providers like Ollama, LM Studio and Apple Intelligence, and supports bring-your-own-key for third-party providers.

Key Features:

- Works Everywhere: any app with a text field

- Grammar and Tone: fix spelling, clarity and style

- Translation: 500+ languages

- Custom Actions and Chains: build multi-step flows

- Local AI and BYOK: Ollama, LM Studio, Apple Intelligence

RewriteBar makes better writing a shortcut away on the Mac, with a free trial and a one-time Standard license at $29.

apps.name: TidyMac
apps.tagline: Find the space your Mac is hiding.
apps.description:
TidyMac shows what fills your disk, System Data included, and clears junk safely in one scan. A ring chart splits System Data into named categories such as caches, backups, simulators, app data and logs, each with a safety rating, and folder sizes are measured the way APFS stores them so totals match Disk Utility. Space Map gives a clickable treemap of your folders, and plain-English search turns requests into Spotlight searches with live sizes. Cleaning finds junk, leftovers, old installers, duplicates and large files, but nothing is removed until you approve, items go to the Trash first and every clean can be undone from History. An app uninstaller, a menu bar free-space readout and an MCP server for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor are included.

Key Features:

- System Data Explained: named categories with safety ratings

- Accurate Sizes: matches Disk Utility totals

- Space Map: clickable treemap of your folders

- Safe Cleaning: approve first, Trash first, undo anytime

- Uninstaller and MCP: remove apps and let agents inspect storage

TidyMac reveals and recovers hidden disk space safely, for a one-time launch price of $9.99 covering two Macs.

apps.name: Upto
apps.tagline: Every app on your Mac, up to date.
apps.description:
Upto finds every app on your Mac, checks each source for newer versions and installs updates with one click. It lists apps from the App Store, Sparkle, Homebrew, TestFlight, Setapp and direct downloads in one place, and tracks command-line tools installed through Homebrew, npm, pipx, uv and more. For apps without an update source it finds one, shows release notes translated on your Mac, and lets you choose stable releases only, include betas or use automatic channels. You can update everything at once, being asked only about major versions, with Touch ID replacing per-app prompts, and every update is verified by signature or checksum and installed in place. Scheduled checks, menu bar access, notifications, skip and ignore options, retry for failed updates and Sweeper integration round it out.

Key Features:

- One List for All Apps: App Store, Sparkle, Homebrew, Setapp and more

- CLI Tools Too: Homebrew, npm, pipx and uv

- Update All: one click with Touch ID approval

- Verified Installs: signature and checksum checks

- Release Notes and Channels: translated notes, stable or beta

Upto keeps every app and tool on your Mac current, priced at $14.99 a year or $39 once during its launch offer.

apps.name: OpenShelf
apps.tagline: Drag, tap, done.
apps.description:
OpenShelf is a Mac app for converting, editing and sharing files while you drag them. Hold Shift while dragging to open the Convert wheel, Shift-Option for Tools or Control for Actions, or press Control-Option-Space for files selected in Finder. It converts images, PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, slides, audio, video, subtitles, archives and folders, including Pages, Numbers and Keynote files. Tools include compress, crop, resize, annotate, redact, remove background, trim video, OCR and combining images into a PDF, while actions cover floating shelves, AirDrop, move, copy path and open in Terminal. Watched folders can add new files to shelves or convert them automatically, results are saved beside originals and nothing is overwritten. It runs offline with no telemetry and can install ffmpeg, LibreOffice and Pandoc in one click.

Key Features:

- Drag Wheels: convert, edit or act on files mid-drag

- Wide Format Support: images, docs, media, archives and iWork

- Built-In Tools: compress, crop, redact, OCR and more

- Floating Shelves and Watched Folders: automate repeat jobs

- Offline and Safe: no telemetry, originals never overwritten

OpenShelf turns every file drag into a quick action, completely free and open source under the MIT license.

apps.name: Stripix
apps.tagline: Convert, clean and shrink photos on any device.
apps.description:
Stripix is an offline photo and PDF tool for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android that does all its processing on your device, even in Airplane Mode. It converts HEIC, PNG and RAW to JPG, WebP or AVIF, one file or hundreds at once, and removes either location data only or all metadata like camera model and dates. Photos can be compressed to an exact file size such as 200 KB, resized by pixels, percentage or preset, and watermarked with text or a logo. PDF tools turn photos into PDFs, merge, split, compress and password-protect documents and convert PDFs to JPG, and you can copy text from images and scans. Repeated steps can be saved as workflows and run from the Share menu or Shortcuts.

Key Features:

- Batch Conversion: HEIC, PNG and RAW to JPG, WebP or AVIF

- Metadata Removal: strip location or all photo details

- Exact-Size Compression: hit precise file sizes

- PDF Toolkit: create, merge, split, compress and protect

- Workflows: save and rerun steps from Share or Shortcuts

Stripix is a private, all-in-one photo and PDF utility across your devices, free for basic use with Pro at $19.99 a year or $39.99 lifetime.

apps.name: MacDisk
apps.tagline: Make some room.
apps.description:
MacDisk is a tidy little cleaner that finds the caches, Xcode leftovers, old iPhone backups and duplicate files filling your disk. You review every item before anything moves, and cleaned items go to the Trash first. Smart Scan checks caches, logs, Xcode data and the Trash together and preselects safe items, while dedicated sections cover system junk, developer junk like DerivedData, simulators, Gradle and npm caches, and old installers in Downloads. An uninstaller removes apps along with their caches, settings and support files, and App Leftovers finds files from apps you've already deleted. Large Files lists your biggest files with nothing preselected, Duplicates compares by content and keeps the oldest copy, and a menu bar view shows free space, junk ready to clean, memory use and low-disk alerts.

Key Features:

- Smart Scan: caches, logs, Xcode data and Trash in one pass

- Developer Junk: DerivedData, simulators, Gradle and npm caches

- Uninstaller and Leftovers: remove apps and their traces

- Large Files and Duplicates: find what takes up space

- Menu Bar Monitor: free space, junk and low-disk alerts

MacDisk is a friendly, careful way to free up space on your Mac, with early prices from $3 and a regular one-time price of $19.

apps.name: Syncophant
apps.tagline: Remote storage that feels local.
apps.description:
Syncophant mounts your remote storage right in Finder, so SFTP, WebDAV, S3-compatible, SMB, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box and Google Drive folders open just like local ones. Files download only when you open them, and you can keep chosen folders available offline, with a default cache of 5 GB per storage that never removes unfinished uploads. Uploads are verified with SHA-256 checksums, interrupted uploads resume and the queue survives restarts, and conflicting edits keep both copies. Deletes can be undone on storage that offers a trash, every file shows its sync status, and a menu bar app keeps you informed. Guided setup is included for Hetzner Storage Boxes, credentials are stored in the Keychain and no telemetry is recorded.

Key Features:

- Finder Integration: remote storage as a normal Finder location

- Many Providers: SFTP, WebDAV, S3, SMB, Dropbox, OneDrive and more

- On-Demand Downloads: files fetched only when opened

- Reliable Uploads: checksums, resume and conflict copies

- Private: Keychain credentials and no telemetry

Syncophant makes cloud and server storage feel local on your Mac, completely free and open source under GPL-3.0.

apps.name: NotchNudge
apps.tagline: See when you'll hit your AI limit.
apps.description:
NotchNudge turns your MacBook's notch into a control centre for AI coding agents. It projects when you'll run out of your Claude Code or Codex session and weekly limits at your current pace, with alerts at 75%, 90% and 100% and when limits reset. A status light shows working, needs-you and done states for each agent with wait times and run durations, and you can Allow or Deny commands right from the notch so nothing runs without a click. A queue lists agents waiting for you, oldest first. Claude Code and Codex get full support, while Cursor and Grok get working and done alerts plus monthly usage. Setup connects on first launch and backs up your settings files, and extras include sound options, jumping to the terminal, a floating pill on non-notch Macs and a one-hour pause.

Key Features:

- Usage Pacing: predicts when you'll hit session and weekly limits

- Agent Status Light: working, needs you and done at a glance

- Allow or Deny: approve commands from the notch

- Waiting Queue: agents needing you, oldest first

- Multi-Agent Support: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Grok

NotchNudge keeps your AI agents and usage limits in check from the notch, for a one-time launch price of $9.99 (regularly $14.99).

apps.name: Tocal
apps.tagline: Todos, clipboard and focus, in your menu bar.
apps.description:
Tocal is a small Mac menu bar app that handles the little things with three tools: todos, clipboard history and a focus timer. Press Control-Option-Command-T in any app to open it, type and press Return. Todos can be reordered by dragging, assigned to days through a calendar and checked off with a burst of confetti, all from the keyboard. The clipboard saves text, links, code, images and files with the source app and time, lets you search, preview and restore items, moves duplicates to the top and skips password manager entries. Focus sessions run from 10 minutes to 6 hours, turn on Do Not Disturb through Shortcuts, show a countdown in the menu bar and keep time through sleep and restarts. There's no account, cloud or analytics, and your data can be exported as one JSON file.

Key Features:

- Quick Todos: add, reorder and schedule tasks from the keyboard

- Clipboard History: text, links, code, images and files

- Focus Timer: 10 minutes to 6 hours with Do Not Disturb

- Global Shortcut: open from any app with ⌃⌥⌘T

- Private: no account or cloud, JSON export

Tocal keeps your todos, clipboard and focus one click away, for a one-time price of ₹499 with all future updates.

apps.name: DevCleaner
apps.tagline: Your Mac isn't full. Your dev folders are.
apps.description:
DevCleaner is a Mac menu bar app that finds and safely clears developer caches from Xcode, npm, Docker and many more tools. A single scan sizes caches from over 30 tools, including Xcode, Android Studio, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Python, Cargo, Go, Docker, Homebrew and AI apps like Claude, Cursor and Ollama. Each category is labelled Safe, Warning or Danger, safe items are preselected and git-tracked source is always skipped. You can preview the cleanup before anything is deleted, use Quick Clean or pick categories manually, and review a 30-day cleaning history. Project Hibernation archives idle projects into one file and restores them later, and Pro adds Auto Clean, Smart Triggers and custom folders.

Key Features:

- 30+ Tool Scanners: Xcode, npm, Docker, Homebrew, AI apps and more

- Safety Labels: Safe, Warning and Danger categories

- Preview Before Cleaning: see exactly what will be removed

- Project Hibernation: archive idle projects and restore later

- Pro Automation: Auto Clean and Smart Triggers

DevCleaner reclaims gigabytes of developer junk safely, free for scanning and safe cleaning with Pro at $19.99 a year or $59 lifetime.

apps.name: NetworkMonitor
apps.tagline: Every byte. Accounted for.
apps.description:
NetworkMonitor is a macOS menu bar app for live network speed and per-app data usage. It shows download and upload speed in the menu bar, updated twice a second in bytes or bits, and breaks down data use by app for the current connection, grouping helper processes under their parent app. Totals reset per network and at midnight and persist across restarts, while local traffic like AirPlay, NAS backups and media servers is excluded from internet totals. Hotspot mode pauses automatic app updates on mobile hotspots and resumes when you leave, and an on-demand speed test uses Apple's networkQuality tool with ping and jitter. A connections window shows companies, countries and servers on a list or world map, with optional block or allow rules, and history can be viewed by day, week, month or year and exported to CSV.

Key Features:

- Live Speed: upload and download in the menu bar

- Per-App Usage: see which apps use your data

- Hotspot Mode: pause updates on mobile hotspots

- Speed Test and Connections Map: ping, jitter and server locations

- History and CSV Export: daily to yearly usage records

NetworkMonitor gives you full visibility of your Mac's network use, completely free and open source with no account or telemetry.

apps.name: Mate
apps.tagline: Your AI limits, next to the notch.
apps.description:
Mate is a macOS app that shows how much of your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Grok usage remains, right beside the notch. While an agent works, a ring shows your 5-hour session usage and switches to weekly usage above 80%. Hover to see session and weekly limits, reset times and your usage pace, and get alerts at 75%, 90% and 100% plus a notice when a limit resets. A usage window breaks down weekly tokens per agent, monthly tokens per model and estimated API cost, and you can switch between multiple accounts per agent. Mate also keeps your Mac awake while agents run and shows album art and controls for Spotify or Music. It uses your existing CLI logins, sends no telemetry and runs natively in Swift using under 30 MB of memory.

Key Features:

- Usage Ring: live session and weekly limits by the notch

- Six Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot and Grok

- Limit Alerts: warnings at 75%, 90% and 100%

- Token and Cost Stats: per agent, per model and estimated cost

- Keep Awake and Music: stays awake while agents work

Mate keeps your AI coding limits in view at a glance, completely free and open source under the MIT license.

apps.name: Lisorto
apps.tagline: Your Mac, sorted. Any file, found.
apps.description:
Lisorto is an AI file organizer and search app for Mac. It reads the files in a folder, proposes a Space and a clear name for each, and moves nothing until you approve, with a single Undo reversing a whole batch. AutoPilot sorts new files in the folders you choose as they arrive, and clear naming renames scans and screenshots based on what they show. Search finds files by name or the text inside them, including scans and screenshots, and Pro extends it to Documents, Desktop and iCloud Drive and finds photos by their content. With Apple Intelligence you can ask questions and get answers with their source files, and a Free up space tool lists installers, copies and large unused files. Every move is logged, nothing is deleted or overwritten, and files are read on your Mac with cloud AI off by default.

Key Features:

- AI Tidy Up: proposes folders and names, moves only on approval

- AutoPilot: sorts new files automatically as they arrive

- Deep Search: find files by name or text inside, even scans

- Ask Your Files: answers with sources via Apple Intelligence

- Safe History and Undo: every move logged and reversible

Lisorto keeps your Mac's files tidy and easy to find, free for manual tidy-ups with Pro at $4.99 a month, $29 a year or a one-time purchase from $29.

apps.name: Mowji
apps.tagline: The native emoji picker for Mac.
apps.description:
