Mowji is a native, keyboard-first emoji picker for Mac. Type a colon and a word like :smile, choose the emoji and keep typing, in apps like Slack, Finder, Safari, Mail and Notion. Search understands everyday words, typos and combined terms, runs on your Mac and works offline, and the picker learns from the emoji you use most. You can save up to 30 favourites and reorder them by dragging, create custom aliases with your own words, hide emoji you never want to see and set a preferred skin tone. The trigger character is customisable, and an expandable full emoji browser lets you copy to the clipboard or add favourites right from the picker.

Key Features:

- Type to Pick: :smile style shortcuts in any app

- Smart Search: understands typos and everyday words

- Favourites: save and reorder up to 30 emoji

- Custom Aliases: create your own emoji shortcuts

- Personal Touches: skin tone, hidden emoji and custom trigger

Mowji makes adding emoji on the Mac fast and fun, with 150 free insertions to try and a one-time launch price of $5 (then $8) for up to 3 devices.

apps.name: Snapzy
apps.tagline: A powerful suite of tools, refined for simplicity.
apps.description:
Snapzy is a native macOS app for screenshots and screen recordings. It captures an area, the active window or the full display with smart element snapping, handles scrolling capture for webpages and long documents, and includes a delay timer for menus and hover states. Subject capture removes backgrounds, you can draw markup on screen before capturing, and a precision magnifier shows a pixel grid and copies RGB or HEX colours. Screen recording includes system audio and microphone. A built-in editor adds arrows, text, highlights and backgrounds, while a video and GIF editor trims clips, adds zoom effects and exports MP4 or GIF. A floating preview, pin to screen, auto-redaction, on-device OCR and a searchable local capture history complete the toolkit.

Key Features:

- Versatile Capture: area, window, full screen and scrolling

- Screen Recording: with system audio and microphone

- Image Editor: arrows, text, highlights and backgrounds

- Video and GIF Editor: trim, zoom and export

- OCR and History: copy text from captures and search past shots

Snapzy is a polished screenshot and recording suite for the Mac, completely free and open source with optional donations.

apps.name: GSD Task Manager
apps.tagline: Get the right things done.
apps.description:
GSD Task Manager is a free, privacy-first task manager built around the Eisenhower Matrix, available on Mac, iPhone, iPad and the web. Every task lands in one of four quadrants, Do First, Schedule, Delegate or Eliminate, so you always know what deserves your attention. You can capture tasks quickly, set priorities, check them off and move them between quadrants, while a progress dashboard shows your productivity metrics. Data is stored locally with no account required, and optional sync with Google, GitHub or Apple sign-in can be turned on and even self-hosted with Docker. It works offline, exports and imports JSON, has no analytics or ads, and offers iPhone widgets, share-sheet input, keyboard-first commands on Mac and an MCP server so AI assistants can manage your tasks.

Key Features:

- Eisenhower Matrix: Do First, Schedule, Delegate and Eliminate

- Progress Dashboard: track your productivity metrics

- Local-First: no account, works offline

- Optional Sync: Google, GitHub or Apple sign-in, self-hostable

- MCP Server: let AI assistants list and create tasks

GSD Task Manager brings calm, focused prioritisation to every device, completely free with no ads or paid tier.

apps.name: Meowse
apps.tagline: Your mouse, but better.
apps.description:
Meowse is an all-in-one mouse app for your Mac's menu bar that improves how your mouse works and keeps your Mac awake. It turns mouse wheel notches into smooth glides in every app, reverses the wheel separately from the trackpad, and lets you speed up, slow down, reshape or turn off acceleration for external mice. Side buttons can go back and forward in apps or trigger shortcuts, and modifier keys let Option scroll faster, Shift scroll sideways and Command skip smoothing. Games and 3D tools can be excluded, while trackpads and the Magic Mouse are left alone. A Keep Awake feature holds your Mac awake for 15 minutes to 4 hours, until a set time or indefinitely, even with the lid closed, and Wiggle Cursor nudges the pointer when you're idle. It uses under 9 MB of memory and 0% CPU when idle.

Key Features:

- Smooth Scrolling: silky glides for any mouse wheel

- Independent Reverse Scroll: separate from the trackpad

- Acceleration Control: reshape or disable mouse acceleration

- Side Buttons and Modifiers: back, forward and custom shortcuts

- Keep Awake: stop sleep for set times, even with the lid closed

Meowse makes any mouse feel at home on the Mac, completely free with public source code and no account or ads.

apps.name: Speechy
apps.tagline: Talk to your apps, right from the notch.
apps.description:
Speechy is private, on-device dictation for your Mac. Hold Fn, speak, and the text appears at your cursor in any app, with transcription running on your Mac and no internet needed after setup. An 'Only my voice' mode learns your voice and filters out nearby speakers, and the output is cleaned up automatically, removing filler words, handling self-corrections, adding punctuation and formatting lists, numbers, dates and emails. Say 'scratch that' to delete your last sentence, and use a personal dictionary, word replacements and snippets to make it your own. It supports ten languages with optional auto-detection, and can connect to over 1,000 apps like Gmail, Slack, Notion and Google Calendar so you can ask questions or take actions from the notch, with a few seconds to undo sends.

Key Features:

- Dictate Anywhere: hold Fn and speak into any app

- Fully On-Device: audio never uploaded, works offline

- Only My Voice: filters out other speakers

- Clean Output: removes fillers and formats text automatically

- App Actions: act on Gmail, Slack, Notion and more from the notch

Speechy is a fast, private voice keyboard for Apple silicon Macs, with a free tier, Pro at $12.99 a month and a lifetime option from $99.

apps.name: Slashspace
apps.tagline: The AI canvas for connecting ideas.
apps.description:
Slashspace is an AI canvas for Mac, Windows and Linux that lets you branch any AI chat on an infinite canvas. Fork a reply from any selected line to explore a tangent without losing the main thread, and attach PDFs, YouTube videos, web pages and notes so chats can read the full sources. Orchestrator mode takes a goal, plans the work, creates and connects canvas nodes and delegates to subagents. You can run Claude Code, Codex or Cursor on your own subscriptions, or add API keys for many providers and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Integrations with Notion, GitHub, Gmail and more come through Composio and MCP, and you can compare Claude, GPT, Gemini and local models side by side and switch models in one click.

Key Features:

- Branching Chats: fork any reply into a new thread on the canvas

- Rich Context: attach PDFs, videos, web pages and notes

- Orchestrator Mode: AI plans work and delegates to subagents

- Bring Your Own Keys: use your subscriptions or API keys

- Multi-Model and Integrations: compare models and connect apps via MCP

Slashspace is a powerful visual workspace for thinking with AI, priced at $89 a year or $249 for a lifetime license.

apps.name: Cinch
apps.tagline: Reminders, made beautiful.
apps.description:
Cinch is a native app for Mac, iPhone and Apple Watch that works on top of your existing Apple Reminders and Calendar, so there's nothing to import or migrate. It reads your current lists, works with Siri, and adds time-of-day views, natural language input and your calendar events alongside tasks. Widgets for the iPhone Lock Screen and Mac desktop, plus Apple Watch complications, let you complete tasks without opening the app. You can organise with #tags and @contacts and filter in one tap, and the Mac app adds keyboard shortcuts, drag-and-drop list management and bulk selection. A command-line tool lets you create, update and complete reminders from Terminal, scripts or AI agents, and proximity filtering and geofenced alerts help with location-based tasks. Built in Swift with EventKit, it uses no third-party servers and your data stays in iCloud.

Key Features:

- Works With Apple Reminders: no import, Siri compatible

- Smart Views: time-of-day views, natural language and events

- Widgets Everywhere: Lock Screen, desktop and Apple Watch

- Tags and Contacts: #tags and @mentions with one-tap filters

- CLI and Automation: manage reminders from Terminal or AI agents

Cinch makes Apple Reminders a joy to use across Mac, iPhone and Apple Watch, free to download with optional in-app upgrades.

apps.name: Tack+
apps.tagline: The notch app for Mac, at the edge of your screen.
apps.description:
Tack+ turns the top or bottom edge of your Mac's screen into a panel that opens when you push the cursor against it. It brings fifteen built-in apps into that panel, including Spotify or Apple Music, Messages, Calendar, Mail, Safari, Reminders, Notes, Contacts, Shortcuts and clipboard history, plus nine widgets like Weather, a CPU and memory monitor, To Do, GitHub, Google Calendar, clocks and countdowns. Hold a shortcut to dictate and the text appears wherever your cursor is, in nine languages transcribed on your Mac. It can transcribe Zoom, Teams and FaceTime calls without a bot joining, and offers an optional local AI assistant on Apple silicon that asks before changing anything. Unified search, a file shelf, a focus timer, Face Lock and a colour picker round it out.

Key Features:

- Edge Panel: push the cursor to the screen edge to open it

- 15 Built-In Apps: music, Messages, Mail, Calendar and more

- Widgets: weather, system monitor, GitHub, clocks and countdowns

- Voice Dictation and Call Transcripts: on-device, no bots

- Local AI Assistant: optional helper that asks before acting

Tack+ packs a whole toolkit into the edge of your Mac screen, with a 3-day free trial and then $4.99 a month for all features on all your Macs.

apps.name: Consul
apps.tagline: Rename to convert.
apps.description:
Consul is a Mac menu bar app that converts files the moment you change their extension. Rename photo.heic to photo.jpg or song.wav to song.mp3 and Consul quietly does the conversion for images, video, audio and documents. Add suffixes to do more: +min shrinks images, videos, audio and PDFs, +5mb targets a size under 5 MB, +mute removes video audio and +speed2x speeds up a clip. It can also crop, rotate and remove backgrounds from images, and transcribe audio and video to text or subtitles on-device. Consul watches your Desktop, Downloads, external drives or the whole system, lets you set quality, codecs and metadata, and keeps backups of originals so any conversion can be undone. Everything is processed locally with no uploads or tracking.

Key Features:

- Rename to Convert: change the extension and the file converts

- Smart Suffixes: +min, +5mb, +mute and +speed2x

- Image Tools: crop, rotate and remove backgrounds

- On-Device Transcription: audio and video to text or subtitles

- Safe Undo: originals backed up, everything processed locally

Consul is a clever, invisible file converter for the Mac, priced at $19 one-time for one Mac or $29 for three.

apps.name: Buffer
apps.tagline: Clipboard history, always at hand.
apps.description:
Buffer is a small, privacy-focused clipboard manager for macOS that lives in your menu bar and keeps all data on your Mac. It automatically saves the text and images you copy and lets you find anything instantly with fuzzy search across your whole history. Built-in Vision OCR extracts text from images offline, and an image canvas lets you pinch to zoom and pan. You can organise clips with colour-coded tags filterable with #, star bookmarks to protect items from automatic removal, pin favourites and select several items to paste at once. Snippets can be edited inline with auto-save, history can be capped at 200, 1,000 or unlimited items with duplicate filtering, and a shortcut sheet and configurable global hotkey keep everything keyboard friendly.

Key Features:

- Clipboard History: saves copied text and images automatically

- Fuzzy Search: find any past clip instantly

- Offline OCR: pull text out of images with Apple Vision

- Tags, Bookmarks and Pins: organise and protect important clips

- Multi-Select and Inline Editing: paste several items and edit in place

Buffer is a lightweight, private clipboard manager for the Mac, completely free and open source under the MIT license.

apps.name: Quilt
apps.tagline: Everything on your screen, finally yours to keep.
apps.description:
Quilt is a native macOS app that turns screen captures into searchable PDFs and image sets. It captures windows or custom areas, scrolls and stitches long content into a single image, and can advance through pages automatically with key presses or mouse clicks, stopping on its own when the pages stop changing. That makes it ideal for saving long articles, slide decks, web-based books and documentation you want to keep. After capturing, you can reorder, crop, annotate and redact pages, then export them as PDF, GIF, ZIP or PNG, JPEG, WEBP and HEIC images. The Pro versions add on-device OCR for searchable text, chapter bookmarks, PDF compression, filename templates, background capture and MCP access so AI agents can work with your captures.

Key Features:

- Window and Area Capture: grab exactly what you need

- Scroll and Auto-Page Capture: stitch long pages and flip through books

- Edit Before Export: reorder, crop, annotate and redact

- Flexible Exports: PDF, GIF, ZIP and multiple image formats

- Pro OCR and MCP: searchable text, bookmarks and AI agent access

Quilt makes it easy to keep anything on your screen as a clean, searchable file, free for up to 15 shots per capture with Pro from $32.99 one-time.

apps.name: NotchMemo
apps.tagline: Make your Mac notch actually useful.
apps.description:
NotchMemo is a private macOS app that puts productivity tools in the notch at the top of your screen, so you can talk to it, glance at it and paste from it. Hold fn to ask questions, dictate into any text field or run voice actions like drafting messages and emails, which you always send yourself. Its dictation cleans up speech, and it can transcribe calls on your Mac and save summaries, action items and transcripts as Markdown. A day timeline shows worked time, breaks and app use for up to 30 days, and break reminders pause when you step away. Screenshots are copied automatically to a shelf, clipboard history is searchable and skips passwords, and extras include notification history, a teleprompter, music controls, AirDrop, an evening recap, themes and a companion character called Memo. It works with Apple Intelligence or your own AI keys, needs no account and keeps your data in a local database.

Key Features:

- Voice in the Notch: ask, dictate and run voice actions with fn

- Meeting Notes: on-device call transcripts saved as Markdown

- Day Timeline and Breaks: worked time, app use and reminders

- Screenshot Shelf and Clipboard: searchable history that skips passwords

- Handy Extras: teleprompter, music, AirDrop and notification history

NotchMemo turns the notch into a private voice, clipboard and focus hub, with a one-time price of $19 (often on sale for $9) and no subscription.

apps.name: NotchTime
apps.tagline: The Screen Time alternative for Mac.
apps.description:
NotchTime is a Screen Time alternative for Mac that lives in your notch and knows when you're actually watching, not just when a tab is open. Hover over the notch to see a focus timer, your time toward a daily goal and how long you've spent in the current app or site. On websites, a small panel appears at each full hour and closes after seven seconds, counting only the time you really watch. A timeline shows each day as a strip, each week as lanes and each month as a grid, while insights track focus and distraction trends over 7, 30 or 90 days with a 0-100 Day Score. Goals warn you from the notch and then block an app or site by hiding it, and Focus and Morning locks keep distractions paused. You can sort apps into focus, neutral and distraction buckets, track pickups and quiet hours, and all data stays on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Notch Glance: focus timer, daily goal and current app time

- Hourly Nudges: short reminders that count real watch time

- Timeline and Insights: day, week and month views with a Day Score

- Goals and Locks: warn, then block distracting apps and sites

- Private by Design: hidden from screen sharing, data stays local

NotchTime brings honest, gentle screen-time tracking to your Mac's notch for a one-time price of $5 with lifetime updates.

apps.name: Tapformat
apps.tagline: Tap ⇧⌘. Convert anything.
apps.description:
Tapformat is a Mac app for converting and shrinking files right from Finder. Select a file, press Shift-Command, and a ring appears showing only the formats that file can become, so you pick one and the new copy is saved beside the original. It converts photos, PDFs, documents, audio and video, and can shrink a file while keeping its format. Quick tools crop to 1:1, 4:5, 16:9 or 9:16 with a smart crop that keeps the subject in frame, resize to half size, 1080px, 2048px or 4K, rotate and flip photos or PDF pages, mute videos without re-encoding, and merge PDFs or combine images into one PDF. It works on many files at once, supports a custom shortcut, drag and drop and the Finder Services menu, and Undo simply sends the new file to the Trash. Everything runs on your Mac with no uploads, and originals are never overwritten.

Key Features:

- Format Ring: press ⇧⌘ in Finder to see only valid formats

- Convert Anything: photos, PDFs, documents, audio and video

- Shrink and Resize: smaller copies, preset sizes and smart crops

- Quick Edits: rotate, flip, mute video and merge PDFs

- Private and Safe: on-device processing, originals never overwritten

Tapformat makes file conversion a one-tap habit on the Mac, completely free with unlimited conversions.

apps.name: NoDoze
apps.tagline: Your Mac. Still going.
apps.description:
NoDoze is a native menu bar app that keeps your Mac awake for as long as you need, even with the lid closed. Start a session with a timer, an end time or no limit at all, and add 15 minutes at any point. Open-lid sessions can run up to 24 hours and the display can switch off while your work keeps going. On MacBooks, closed-lid mode runs for up to four continuous hours after a one-time, administrator-approved helper setup. Power rules let you require the charger or allow battery use with a cutoff you choose, and sessions stop automatically on critical thermal pressure. It has no telemetry or tracking, stores preferences locally and works offline once activated.

Key Features:

- Flexible Sessions: timer, end time or unlimited

- Closed-Lid Mode: keep MacBooks running with the lid shut

- Display Off: screen sleeps while work continues

- Power Rules: require the charger or set a battery cutoff

- Safe and Private: thermal protection and no tracking

NoDoze is a simple, reliable way to keep your Mac working overnight, with five free sessions and a $4 lifetime license.

apps.name: Stringout
apps.tagline: Camera to timeline for free.
apps.description:
Stringout is a media asset management app for post-production on the Mac that finds the shots, transcribes the interviews and builds the stringout for you, while your footage stays on your own drives. Add pro formats like ARRIRAW, BRAW, R3D and ProRes from a shuttle drive or RAID, and Stringout reads picture and sound in place without moving files. You can search what was shot and what was said across every indexed drive, describing a frame or typing half a line of dialogue, with on-device AI and unlimited private transcription running on your Mac. Auto-assemble syncs picture to sound and builds a first cut from your selects, which you can take straight into Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro. With Pro, File Streaming puts your team's media in Finder for remote editors without shipping drives, and saved versions flow back automatically. It also supports multicam projects, VFX pulls and searching unplugged drives.

Key Features:

- Pro Format Ingest: ARRIRAW, BRAW, R3D and ProRes read in place

- Footage and Transcript Search: describe a shot or type a line of dialogue

- On-Device AI: unlimited private transcription and analysis on your Mac

- Auto-Assemble: synced first cuts sent to Premiere, Resolve or Final Cut Pro

- File Streaming (Pro): team media in Finder for remote editors

Stringout gives editors and assistant editors an AI-powered head start on every project, free to use with Pro at $24 per seat per month for File Streaming and larger libraries.

apps.name: NullKey
apps.tagline: SSH keys in the Enclave.
apps.description:
NullKey is a Mac app that creates SSH keys inside your Mac's Secure Enclave and runs a local SSH agent so ssh and git can authenticate with them. The private key is generated in the Enclave and is non-exportable by hardware design, so it never exists in memory or on disk and can't be copied or stolen; the app can only ask the Enclave to sign. For each key you choose at creation whether every signature needs Touch ID or signs silently while the app runs. Just copy the public key into GitHub, GitLab or authorized_keys, point SSH at the agent with a one-line config, and ssh, git and the GitHub CLI keep working as always. NullKey also includes an Authenticator for 2FA and backup codes sealed in the Secure Enclave, SSH host management, AWS and GCP access, and an activity log of every signature. There's no account, no network access and no data collection.

Key Features:

- Secure Enclave SSH Keys: hardware-backed keys that can never be exported

- Touch ID Signing: require Touch ID per key, or sign silently

- Local SSH Agent: works with ssh, git and the GitHub CLI out of the box

- Authenticator: 2FA and backup codes sealed in the Secure Enclave

- Activity Log: see every signature the agent serves

NullKey brings hardware-grade security to your SSH and 2FA workflow on the Mac, and it's free on the Mac App Store.

apps.name: Seenlio
apps.tagline: Describe the image. Find it on your Mac.
apps.description:
Seenlio is a Mac app that finds images in your folders by describing what's in them or by searching the words inside screenshots. Type something like 'orange flowers in a garden' or 'a white island in a blue ocean' and Seenlio searches what your images show using models that run on your Mac. Text search reads between the pixels, finding quotes, receipts and tiny details in your screenshots with OCR in English, Hindi, Chinese, Japanese and Spanish, and highlights the matching region in the image. A quick search shortcut, Command-Shift-Space, opens your library from anywhere. Your original files stay exactly where they are, and everything works privately and offline after setup.

Key Features:

- Visual Search: find photos by describing colours, objects or scenes

- Text in Images: search the words inside screenshots and photos

- Five-Language OCR: English, Hindi, Chinese, Japanese and Spanish

- Quick Search Shortcut: open your image library from anywhere

- Private and Offline: on-device models, files stay where they are

Seenlio makes it easy to find any image you remember but can't name, with an early-bird one-time price of ₹499 (normally ₹999) for one Mac.

apps.name: Kudu
apps.tagline: Say it once. It's already written.
apps.description:
Kudu is private voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux that turns your voice into clean, formatted writing in any app. Hold a key, speak naturally, even messily with ums, repeats and corrections, and let go, and Kudu writes what you meant. It formats text for the app you're in, so you get mentions in Slack, lists in Notes, proper code in your editor and your own slang with friends. Kudu learns your words, offers a command mode, snippets, a style for every app, a custom shortcut, meeting notes and insights into how much you've written. Speaking at around 150 words a minute is about three times faster than typing, and on an M-series Mac the text typically appears about 0.3 seconds after you let go. Everything is transcribed on your computer with no account, no cloud, no analytics and no telemetry, and it works offline once set up.

Key Features:

- Hold to Talk: hold a key, speak and let go to write in any app

- Clean Formatting: removes filler words and fixes corrections automatically

- App-Aware Styles: mentions, lists, code and casual tone where they fit

- Meeting Notes and Snippets: extra tools for everyday writing

- Fully On-Device: no account, no cloud and works offline

Kudu is a fast, private way to write with your voice across Mac, Windows and Linux, completely free and open source under the MIT license.

apps.name: Tucko
apps.tagline: Your Mac's clipboard. Saved and searchable.
apps.description:
Tucko is a clipboard manager for Mac that saves the text, links, images, code and file references you copy so you can find a previous copy, preview it and paste it again. Press Option-Shift-Space to open a visual shelf of your history, search by text, title or the app a clip came from, and tap Space for a full preview before you paste. Pinboards keep the clips you reuse within reach alongside saved items and reminders, and a handful of copied images can become a moodboard with captions and a colour palette pulled from your references. Text shortcuts let you give any card a code like ;sig and expand it as you type, and you can select several cards and paste them into fields one after another. On macOS 26, Tucko can summarize, rewrite and translate clipboard text with Apple Intelligence, and your history always stays on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Visual Clipboard Shelf: text, links, images, code and files in one place

- Search and Preview: find clips by text, title or app and preview with Space

- Pinboards and Moodboards: keep favourite clips and turn images into boards

- Text Shortcuts: expand codes like ;sig into saved text

- Apple Intelligence: summarize, rewrite and translate copied text

Tucko gives your Mac's clipboard a memory with a beautiful visual shelf, with a 7-day free trial and a founding one-time price of €6.99 (then €9.99).

apps.name: Ratio
apps.tagline: Write it down. It adds up.
apps.description:
Ratio is a notepad calculator for Mac, Windows and Linux that lets you jot down prices, currencies, units and dates the way you would in a note, with the answer appearing beside every line as you type. It supports more than 160 live currencies and the major cryptos, with rates that refresh on their own, so you can mix dollars, euros and pounds in a single line and still get the right total. You can name a number like 'price' and use it anywhere below, or write L3 to bring in the answer from line 3, and everything updates when one value changes. Ratio converts over 150 units, handles time zones and date countdowns, and covers work and money tasks like hours times your rate, VAT, loan payments and working days that skip public holidays. Students get equation solving, integrals, derivatives, exact answers, physical constants and statistics, plus lists and small plots when needed.

Key Features:

- Live Currencies: 160+ currencies and crypto with auto-refreshing rates

- Smart Notes: named variables and line references that update automatically

- Units and Time: 150+ units, time zones and live countdowns

- Work and Money: invoices, VAT, loans and working-day calculations

- School and Science: equations, calculus, constants and statistics

Ratio turns everyday math into simple notes that calculate themselves, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $9.99 price.

apps.name: Winq
apps.tagline: Look. Wink. Done.
apps.description:
Winq turns your Mac's camera into a hands-free input, letting you control your Mac with your eyes and face. Glance at a display or window to focus it, and Winq raises it and puts the pointer where you're looking so your next keystroke lands there. Raise your eyebrows to turn on scroll mode and look toward the top or bottom of the window to scroll, then wink with your left eye to left-click or your right eye to right-click, while normal blinks are ignored. Ten facial gestures like nods, tilts and smiles can be bound to any shortcut, globally or per app. Winq is designed both for people with RSI, carpal tunnel or limited hand mobility and for developers who want speed. It lives in your menu bar, needs only a 720p camera at 15 fps, and runs entirely on your Mac, with no frames saved to disk or sent anywhere.

Key Features:

- Gaze Focus: look at a display or window to focus it

- Eyebrow Scroll: raise your eyebrows and look to scroll

- Wink Clicks: left and right winks for left and right clicks

- Gesture Shortcuts: 10 facial gestures bound to any shortcut

- Fully On-Device: no frames saved or sent anywhere

Winq offers a clever hands-free way to control your Mac for accessibility and speed, with a free one-day trial and a one-time $7.87 price.

apps.name: Snipora
apps.tagline: Write it once. Type it in four keys.
apps.description:
Snipora is a text expander for your Mac's menu bar. Type an abbreviation like ;addr in any app and it instantly becomes your address, and the same works for your daily replies, signature and today's date. Snipora pastes snippets instead of typing them, so formatting, emoji and accents survive, your clipboard is restored afterwards, and pressing Esc right after brings the abbreviation back. It notices phrases you keep retyping and offers to make them snippets, counting words in memory only and never saving or sending them. It supports fill-in forms, dates, pattern matching and per-app rules, explains when it can't expand because of Secure Input, and imports from macOS Text Replacements, TextExpander, Espanso, Alfred, Raycast, your Contacts card, CSV and JSON. It's native SwiftUI with no account, and your snippets stay on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Instant Expansion: type short abbreviations to insert full text anywhere

- On-Device Suggestions: offers snippets for phrases you keep typing

- Fill-In Forms and Dates: dynamic snippets with choices and dates

- Per-App Rules: control where snippets expand

- Easy Import: bring snippets from TextExpander, Espanso, Alfred and more

Snipora makes repetitive typing disappear on the Mac, free for up to 15 snippets with a lifetime license at $29.99 for early buyers (then $39.99) or $2.99 a month.

apps.name: Rambla
apps.tagline: Your windows, in a row.
apps.description:
Rambla is a scrolling window manager for macOS that places every window as a column on one horizontal strip that keeps going past the edges of the screen. Instead of cutting your screen into smaller pieces, new windows appear right next to the one you're using at their own size, and the strip slides to whatever you focus with a shortcut, a click, Command-Tab or the Dock. Windows outside the screen peek in from the edge so they're always one click away. You can stack windows in one column or as tabs, pin columns like chat or music to an edge, swipe with three or four fingers to move along the strip, and use an overview to see every window at once. Rambla remembers columns, widths and stacks after restarts, gives every display and desktop its own strip, and is scriptable with rambla:// links, a command-line tool and Raycast scripts. It's native Swift with zero idle CPU and works alongside Rectangle.

Key Features:

- Horizontal Window Strip: every window becomes a column that slides into view

- Stacks and Tabs: group windows in one column or as tabs

- Pinned Columns: keep chat or music visible at the edge

- Trackpad and Mouse Navigation: swipe or scroll from column to column

- Overview and Memory: see all windows at once and restore layouts after restarts

Rambla brings a fresh, scrolling approach to window management on the Mac, completely free and open source.

apps.name: Tiremusu
apps.tagline: Your notch, reimagined.
apps.description:
Tiremusu lives under your MacBook's notch and watches your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and opencode sessions. It lists every session with its agent, project, branch and what it's doing right now, and Command-1 to 9 opens any of them. When an agent asks for permission or a question, a card drops down with the exact command or options, and you can allow, deny or pick an answer with a keyboard shortcut without your editor losing focus. When a turn ends you can reply right from the notch, and the agent gets a real message and starts again, or jump to the exact app, terminal or pane the session lives in. Phase tabs show how each turn split between researching, reasoning, writing and reviewing, a small character reacts to your agents' state, and usage limits for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor are always visible. There's no account and no telemetry.

Key Features:

- All Agents in One Place: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and opencode sessions

- Answer from the Keyboard: allow, deny or pick options without switching apps

- Reply and Jump: send a one-line reply or jump to the session's window

- Live Turn Detail: phase tabs, tool calls, tokens and model info

- Usage Limits: 5-hour, weekly and monthly limits at a glance

Tiremusu keeps you in control of every AI coding agent from the notch, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $9.99 lifetime license.

apps.name: Papa
apps.tagline: Your Mac has a notch. Now it has a dad.
apps.description:
Papa is a Mac notch app with an Indian dad's personality that keeps you accountable through the day. Every morning he asks for your plan with three things to do, and every evening he checks what got done. He calls out YouTube rabbit holes and other time-wasting sites with the full Sharma ji ladder, reminds you about your battery and charger, and shows a notch dashboard in English or Hinglish. With Pro, Papa reacts to your sales from Stripe and Dodo Payments with today's revenue and MRR, brings out the belt on zero-sale evenings, and adds focus mute, nine streaks, approval levels and rewards like the ₹10 note and ladoo. You can set quiet hours, a day off and a daily cap so he never overdoes it.

Key Features:

- Morning Plan: three things to do, every day

- Evening Check-In: Papa asks what actually got done

- Time-Waster Callouts: nudges when you drift to distracting sites

- Sales Reactions: celebrates Stripe and Dodo Payments revenue (Pro)

- Streaks and Rewards: approval levels, streaks and fun rewards (Pro)

Papa adds a funny, motivating dose of accountability to your Mac, free to use with a one-time Pro unlock at $4.99 for early buyers (then $9.99).

apps.name: Lynx Download Manager
apps.tagline: The download manager that lives in your notch.
apps.description:
Lynx is a download manager for Mac that lives in your notch. Copy a link and the notch offers it, letting you download the whole file or just the minutes you need. Every download is split across up to 32 connections for up to twice the speed of your browser, up to 10 downloads run at once, and they resume after sleep, a restart or dropped Wi-Fi. The Lynx button sits on videos in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc so you can pick a quality or choose Clip to save only a part, as a video, a vertical or square clip, a GIF or audio. Paste a playlist to save every video, see each quality with its file size from 4K down to 480p, and use the notch for your music, a shelf and your clipboard. Your links stay on your Mac and there's no account.

Key Features:

- Notch Downloads: copy a link and download it from the notch

- 32 Connections: faster downloads that resume after interruptions

- Clip Just a Part: save only the seconds you need as video, GIF or audio

- Browser Button: download videos from Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc

- Playlists and Qualities: grab whole playlists in the quality you choose

Lynx makes downloading on the Mac faster and smarter, with every Pro feature free for two weeks, free file downloads forever with Lynx Basic, and Pro available monthly, yearly or as a lifetime purchase.

apps.name: Make Mac Better
apps.tagline: Nine apps in one. Everything your Mac is missing.
apps.description:
Make Mac Better is an all-in-one Mac app that bundles nine tools into one purchase. It adds strip and tiling window management, a second dock with apps and working widgets, and 38 utilities for video, audio, images, PDF and on-device AI. A files module sorts your files, cleans up and offers natural-language search, while Transfer moves photos from your phone to your Mac with a QR code and no cables. Captures lets you take screenshots, annotate them and add a background like a pro, Awake keeps your AI working even with the lid closed, and the Notch module puts your day, music, AI and more in the notch. Everything runs on your Mac with no subscription, and the site includes a playground to try modules before you buy.

Key Features:

- Window Management: strip and tiling layouts with stable widths

- Second Dock: apps and working widgets in an extra dock

- 38 Tools: video, audio, image, PDF and on-device AI utilities

- Files and Transfer: sort files and send phone photos via QR code

- Captures, Awake and Notch: screenshots, keep-awake and a smart notch

Make Mac Better replaces a stack of utilities with one app, at a launch price of €4 (normally €19.99) with a 5-day money-back guarantee.

apps.name: Kopi
apps.tagline: Everything you copy, on every computer.
apps.description:
Kopi is an open-source clipboard manager for macOS and Windows that keeps everything you copy, searchable in a keystroke. It saves unlimited history of text, links, images, colours and code, so nothing gets lost to the next copy, and instant search lets you find something you copied last week and narrow it down by type or by the app it came from. Pinboards keep the replies, addresses and snippets you reuse in boards that stay put, one shortcut away. If you work across a Mac and a PC, Kopi can sync your clipboard between them over your local network, end-to-end encrypted and entirely optional. You can paste as plain text to drop stray formatting, and the whole app is keyboard-first with shortcuts you can change.

Key Features:

- Unlimited History: text, links, images, colours and code saved as you copy

- Instant Search: find any clip by text, type or source app

- Pinboards: keep reusable replies and snippets one shortcut away

- Mac and Windows Sync: encrypted local-network clipboard sync

- Paste as Plain Text: strip formatting so pastes match where they land

Kopi is a private, cross-platform clipboard manager for Mac and Windows, free and open source during its alpha.

apps.name: WakeBee
apps.tagline: Your Mac. Stays awake.
apps.description:
WakeBee is a menu bar app that keeps your Mac awake while your AI agents and long jobs keep working, even with the lid closed. Pick a time and press start, and a green dot in your menu bar shows your session is running. With closed-lid mode, a small helper lets you close your MacBook once WakeBee says it's ready, and the session keeps going. Battery and power controls let you require a charger or run on battery down to a cutoff you set, so your Mac never drains completely. Your preferences stay on your Mac, everything is a click away in the menu bar, and it works on Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later.

Key Features:

- Timed Sessions: keep your Mac awake for exactly as long as you need

- Closed-Lid Mode: keep working with your MacBook lid closed

- Battery Controls: require a charger or set a battery cutoff

- Menu Bar Status: a green dot shows when a session is running

- Private and Simple: preferences stay on your Mac

WakeBee keeps your Mac working while you step away, with an early-bird lifetime license of $9 for up to three Macs and a 14-day money-back guarantee.

apps.name: Budget Day
apps.tagline: Track every dollar right where you work.
apps.description:
Budget Day is a native Mac app that tracks every account and currency and shows what's coming before it lands. A calm dashboard answers one question, how am I doing this month, with your savings ratio at the top and income, expenses, savings and net worth one glance away. Subscriptions and bills appear on a schedule you can view across one month, three months, six months or a year, with recurring rules and logos for services like Netflix and Apple. Keep a dollar account next to a rupee account and Budget Day converts everything into one net worth total, with transfers between accounts and scheduled and completed payments per account. You can search transactions by name, category or note, set savings goals in any currency with progress bars, choose from four themes and check your numbers from the menu bar or desktop widgets.

Key Features:

- Monthly Dashboard: savings ratio, income, expenses and net worth at a glance

- Upcoming Payments: subscriptions and bills scheduled up to a year ahead

- Multi-Currency Accounts: one net worth across every currency

- Savings Goals: track progress toward targets in any currency

- Menu Bar and Widgets: check totals and next payments without opening the app

Budget Day makes personal finance calm and clear on the Mac, with a one-time purchase for one Mac and no subscription.

apps.name: FilesMac
apps.tagline: A calm file manager and editor for your Mac.
apps.description:
FilesMac is a native macOS file manager and code editor that lets you browse like Finder, open any folder as a project and edit right where you are. Every tab is either a Finder view for getting around or an Explorer view for getting things done, and you can switch whenever the job changes. The Finder view brings tabs with a tactile animated tab bar, list and icon views sorted your way, Quick Look with Space, Go to Folder with Tab completion, Connect to Server for SMB, AFP, NFS, FTP and WebDAV, favourites, bookmarks and Trash with Put Back. The Explorer view opens a folder as a project with a file tree, syntax highlighting and live previews, so you can edit files without switching apps. It's small, fast and universal for Apple silicon and Intel on macOS 12 or later.

Key Features:

- Finder View: tabs, list and icon views, Quick Look and Go to Folder

- Explorer View: open any folder as a project with a file tree

- Built-In Editor: syntax highlighting and live previews

- Network Locations: connect to SMB, AFP, NFS, FTP and WebDAV servers

- Bookmarks and Favorites: jump to the places you visit most

FilesMac combines a calm file browser and a lightweight editor in one native app, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $5 lifetime license.

apps.name: HeartbeatMac
apps.tagline: Your Mac's heartbeat, app by app.
apps.description:
HeartbeatMac is an Activity Monitor alternative for Mac that groups every process under the app it belongs to, so a thousand processes become a hundred apps. Instead of a hundred entries called Google Chrome Helper, you get one figure per app for CPU, memory, energy, disk, network and GPU, with helpers included, and you can expand any app or switch to a flat process list. Live charts cover CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU and battery, and 30 days of history show the last hour, day, week or month for every metric along with which apps used the most. HeartbeatMac sends alerts when something misbehaves, flags idle dev servers with how long they've done nothing and the memory they'd free, and puts a compact monitor in your menu bar. You can quit or force quit an app or a single process, and it always asks first.

Key Features:

- Grouped by App: every helper process counted under its parent app

- Live Charts: CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU and battery at a glance

- 30-Day History: see trends and top apps for any period

- Smart Alerts: get notified when apps misbehave or dev servers sit idle

- Menu Bar Monitor: keep an eye on your Mac without opening a window

HeartbeatMac gives you a clearer picture of what's slowing your Mac, with a 7-day free trial and a $5 launch price (then $29) for up to three Macs.

apps.name: HocusFocus
apps.tagline: A little magic for your Mac.
apps.description:
HocusFocus is a launcher for macOS 26 with Apple's private on-device AI built in. Press Option-Space and just type: apps, answers, plain-English commands and AI, all from one little box. Fuzzy search finds apps from a few keystrokes and learns what you open most, and anything that doesn't match becomes a web search. Instant answers appear before you finish typing, covering math the way you write it, live currency conversion with daily ECB rates, around 80 units, world clocks, date counts and hex or binary conversion. Everyday requests like 'open figma', 'quit slack' or 'its too loud in here, turn it down a bit' are understood by fast, predictable rules that work offline, and anything else goes to the language model built into macOS. Clipboard history, notes and wallpaper themes are one tab away.

Key Features:

- Fuzzy App Launcher: open any app from a few keystrokes

- Instant Answers: math, currency, units, time zones and date counts

- Plain-English Commands: control your Mac by just saying what you want

- On-Device AI: Apple's private language model answers your questions

- Clipboard, Notes and Themes: extra tools one tab away

HocusFocus is a fast, magical Spotlight and Raycast alternative for macOS 26, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $5 price.

apps.name: Annotake
apps.tagline: Show any AI exactly what you see.
apps.description:
Annotake is a Mac menu bar app for showing an AI exactly what you see. Double-tap your key, click through anything in any app, and Annotake records each step as a screenshot captioned with what you clicked. When you're done, drag the card straight into ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or anything else that takes images. Frames are picked by comparing pixels and captions come from macOS Accessibility, so there are no AI models and no uploads involved. Each recording is saved as a folder of PNGs and a steps.md file in your Pictures folder and clears out after 30 days unless you choose to keep it. Annotake only sees your screen while you record and never records what you type.

Key Features:

- One-Key Recording: double-tap a key to start and stop

- Captioned Steps: every click becomes a captioned screenshot

- Drag into Any AI: drop the card into ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor

- Plain Files: PNGs plus a steps.md saved locally

- Private by Design: no AI models, no uploads and no keystroke recording

Annotake makes it effortless to give AI assistants clear visual context, and it's free during the beta.

apps.name: Cupola
apps.tagline: Your Calendar, Reminders and Notes, finally together.
apps.description:
Cupola is a Mac app that brings your Apple Calendar, Reminders and Notes together in one place, plus a clipboard that remembers, all waiting in your MacBook notch. Hover the notch to see five tabs: Calendar with your week at a glance, Reminders you can tick off with confetti, your real Apple Notes with checklists, clipboard history and a Focus timer you spin like a kitchen timer. Natural-language quick add lets you type things like 'dentist next tuesday 4pm' or 'remind me to water the plants tomorrow', and Cupola figures out the day and time and drops it into Apple Calendar or Reminders. The clipboard manager quietly remembers the text, links, images and files you copy, so you can pin the keepers, search the rest and grab any of it again. Everything stays in sync with Apple's own apps.

Key Features:

- Notch Dashboard: calendar, reminders, notes, clipboard and focus timer

- Natural-Language Quick Add: type events and reminders the way you say them

- Apple Sync: works with your real Calendar, Reminders and Notes

- Clipboard History: pin, search and reuse anything you copied

- Focus Timer: spin the dial and start a focused session

Cupola puts your day one hover away in the MacBook notch, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time lifetime license of $20.

apps.name: TapMac
apps.tagline: Tap your Mac. Start talking.
apps.description:
TapMac feels a tap on your MacBook and turns it into an action, so you can dictate a message, fix your writing or paste from your history without learning a single shortcut. One tap near the trackpad starts voice typing, and your words appear in whatever app you're using, transcribed on your Mac so your audio never leaves it. Two taps on selected text explain it, fix the grammar, rephrase it or summarize it using Apple Intelligence on macOS 26. Three taps open your clipboard history with text, links, images and files ready to paste. You choose what each tap count does, the tap that ends dictation can press Return to send your message hands-free, and smart modes mute calls or pause videos with a single tap. Tappy, a friendly character in your menu bar, shows when a tap lands and when TapMac is listening.

Key Features:

- Tap to Dictate: speak and your words appear in any app

- AI Text Actions: fix, rephrase, explain or summarize selected text

- Clipboard History: three taps to paste what you copied earlier

- Custom Tap Actions: choose what one, two or three taps do

- Smart Modes: mute calls or pause videos with a tap

TapMac makes your MacBook respond to a simple tap, for a one-time $7.99 launch price (then $20) with no subscription.

apps.name: TypeCorrect
apps.tagline: Typed in the wrong layout? Double-tap Shift.
apps.description:
TypeCorrect is a menu bar app for macOS that fixes text typed in the wrong keyboard layout. If you typed 'руддщ' instead of 'hello', just double-tap Shift and TypeCorrect instantly converts what you just typed and switches the layout for you. You can also turn on Smart switch so it handles slips automatically. Instead of selecting, deleting, switching the layout and retyping a whole sentence, which takes around eight seconds each time, the fix takes about one second and happens right in place. It's built for bilingual and multilingual Mac users who switch between alphabets like Latin and Cyrillic all day, and unlike aggressive auto-switchers it won't mess with names, code and links you typed on purpose. TypeCorrect runs on macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon and Intel.

Key Features:

- Double-Tap Shift: instantly fix text typed in the wrong layout

- Automatic Layout Switch: switches to the right layout after fixing

- Smart Switch: optional automatic correction as you type

- Respects Intent: leaves names, code and links alone

- Lightweight Menu Bar App: works in any app on macOS 13+

TypeCorrect saves bilingual typists hours of retyping every year, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $9.90 price.

apps.name: Layout
apps.tagline: Switch projects, not windows.
apps.description:
Layout is a macOS app for developers juggling multiple projects that gives each project its own workspace. Your client work and side projects each keep the right editor, terminals, browser tabs and AI chats together, and you switch between them with one shortcut, holding Option and pressing Tab to choose a workspace. When you switch, the other project's dev servers keep running and its windows wait exactly where you left them. Layout also lets you know when an AI agent like Claude asks for permission in another workspace, so you can jump straight to its chat. It supports multi-display layouts with a visual editor, and a Focus Agent feature arrived in version 0.6. Layout runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 14 or later.

Key Features:

- Project Workspaces: editor, terminals, browser tabs and AI chats together

- One-Shortcut Switching: hold Option and Tab to change projects

- Keeps Things Running: dev servers continue while you switch

- Agent Notifications: know when Claude asks for permission elsewhere

- Multi-Display Editor: arrange workspaces across several screens

Layout keeps multi-project developers focused and organised, with a 14-day free trial and a one-time $9.99 early-access price (instead of $19).

apps.name: Orange
apps.tagline: Convert any file right where it sits.
apps.description:
Orange is a free file converter that lives in your Mac's menu bar. Drag any file, press Shift, and pick a format from a wheel that opens under your pointer, then let go and the converted file appears next to the original. It supports 55 file types including HEIC, PDF, MOV, MP3, Word, PowerPoint and Excel, and free tools like ffmpeg add more formats automatically once installed. You can drop a dozen files on the wheel to convert them all together, use arrow keys, Return or number keys to pick a format without the mouse, and feel haptic ticks on your trackpad as you cross each format. Long video conversions move to a small panel so you can keep working, and every conversion runs on your Mac with nothing uploaded.

Key Features:

- Drag, Shift, Release: convert files with one gesture from the menu bar

- 55 File Types: images, video, audio, PDFs and Office documents

- Batch Conversion: drop many files on the wheel at once

- Keyboard and Haptics: pick formats with keys and feel each selection

- Fully Local: no uploads, with output saved next to the original

Orange makes file conversion on the Mac quick and private, and it's completely free forever.

apps.name: Minimal Paste
apps.tagline: Quick access to your clipboard history and folders.
apps.description:
Minimal Paste is a local-only clipboard manager for Mac that brings everything you copied back in a keystroke. Press Shift-Command-V to open the shelf, use the arrows to move and Return to paste straight into the app you were using. The shelf filters as you type across text, images, links, files and colours, and pinned clips stay put no matter what your retention settings are. You can group clips with a name and colour, select several clips and paste them together, and add any folder, including subfolders such as Downloads or Screenshots, to paste the files inside. Place the shelf on the bottom, left or right edge, attached or floating, or in a window. Password managers are ignored and your history never leaves your Mac, with no account and no iCloud.

Key Features:

- Clipboard History: text, images, links, files and colours a keystroke away

- Pins and Groups: keep favourite clips and organise them by colour

- Folder Shelf: paste files from Downloads, Screenshots or any folder

- Bulk Paste: select several clips and paste them together

- Custom Shelf: bottom, left, right or window, attached or floating

Minimal Paste is a fast, private alternative to pricier clipboard apps, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $9.99 price for up to three Macs.

apps.name: Perchy
apps.tagline: Your notch finally has a job.
apps.description:
Perchy is a native Mac notch app that puts crypto prices and alerts, your music, your calendar, your clipboard and a tray for files in the dead space at the top of your screen. The Markets module shows a crypto price ticker with a scrubbable chart and price alerts that fire once or every time a level is crossed. Music shows artwork, progress and controls for whatever is playing, including YouTube Music in the browser, while Calendar shows today's events with a Join button for Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex and FaceTime calls. Clipboard keeps your recent copies a hover away and skips private ones from password managers, Convert turns amounts between coins and 30 currencies, and Tray lets you park files on the closed notch. Pro adds more coins and alerts, minute-by-minute prices, lyrics, AirPlay switching, a full week of events and Apple Intelligence actions.

Key Features:

- Crypto Markets: live prices, charts and price alerts in the notch

- Music Controls: artwork, progress and playback for any player

- Calendar with Join: today's events and one-click meeting joins

- Clipboard and Tray: recent copies and parked files a hover away

- Currency Converter: coins and 30 currencies at up-to-date rates (Pro)

Perchy turns your MacBook notch into a handy dashboard, free with no time limit and a one-time $14.99 Pro upgrade.

apps.name: Continuo
apps.tagline: One keyboard. Every Mac.
apps.description:
Continuo lets you use one keyboard and mouse across all your Macs on the same local network, over Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Push your pointer past the edge of one screen and keep going onto the next Mac, while each Mac keeps its own display. Unlike Universal Control, your Macs don't need to share an Apple ID, so a work Mac and a personal Mac can sit on one desk together. Continuo also shares your clipboard and files between them, and keyboard, mouse, clipboard and file content stay on an authenticated, encrypted peer connection that never goes through an internet service. It's built to handle sleep gracefully, and Pro adds larger clipboard transfers, pairing more than two Macs, waking a sleeping Mac and typing on a locked Mac. There's no telemetry, no cloud relay and the security code is available for audit.

Key Features:

- Shared Keyboard and Mouse: move seamlessly between Macs

- No Shared Apple ID: works across different accounts

- Clipboard and File Sharing: copy on one Mac, paste on another

- Encrypted Local Connection: nothing goes through the internet

- Pro Extras: more Macs, wake from sleep and larger clipboard transfers

Continuo makes multi-Mac desks feel like one computer, free for two Macs with a one-time $39 Pro upgrade and no subscription.

apps.name: Branchway
apps.tagline: Your files, finally at home.
apps.description:
Branchway is a native Finder alternative for macOS with tabs, dual panes, its own search index, a map of your disk and themes to make it yours. List, icons, columns and gallery views share one selection and one set of shortcuts, and you can split the window into two panes when moving files around, each with its own back, forward and clickable path. Press Command-K and one box takes a folder path, a file name, a command or even a description of a photo, document or video. Branchway keeps its own index of file names on every volume and merges in Spotlight when it's there, so search still works when Spotlight is off or catching up, with filters for scope, kind, date, size and tags. It also includes a Home page, a storage map, folder comparison, sync browsing between panes and support for 16 languages on macOS 14 or later.

Key Features:

- Four Views and Dual Panes: list, icons, columns and gallery with split panes

- Command Palette: jump to paths, files and commands with Command-K

- Own Search Index: fast search even when Spotlight is off

- Storage Map: see what's taking up space on your disk

- Themes and Tabs: unlimited tabs, folder comparison and custom themes

Branchway gives power users a faster, more capable file manager than Finder, with a 14-day free trial and a launch price of $19 (usually $29).

apps.name: Newton
apps.tagline: A puppy for your menu bar.
apps.description:
Newton is a macOS menu bar companion, a cartoon puppy who changes his mood with whatever you're doing while handling a handful of everyday jobs. One switch keeps your Mac and its display awake for half an hour or until you say stop. Newton can cast your screen to the TV with very little lag, encoding frames on your Mac's media engine and encrypting every session with a fresh key, and it can play media on your TV or switch into presentation mode. Newton Drop opens a private page on your Wi-Fi so you can send files to your phone, and clipboard history keeps what you copied an hour ago ready to paste again. Everything stays on your local network with no accounts and no cloud, phone links are secret and expire, and nothing casts to a TV you didn't pick. Not a dog person? Mochi the cat is one setting away.

Key Features:

- Keep Mac Awake: one switch keeps your Mac and display awake

- Cast Your Screen: low-lag, encrypted screen casting to your TV

- Send to Phone: Newton Drop shares files over your Wi-Fi

- Clipboard History: get back things you copied earlier

- Animated Companion: a puppy or a cat whose mood follows what you're doing

Newton turns handy Mac utilities into a charming menu bar pet, and it's free for early users on macOS 14 or later.

apps.name: Tinycast
apps.tagline: Everything on your Mac. One keystroke away.
apps.description:
Tinycast is a small, native launcher for macOS that puts your apps, clipboard, snippets and windows one keystroke away. Find any app by typing a few letters, pin favourites, see what's running and quit or restart apps from the keyboard. A built-in calculator handles math, units, currencies, time zones and dates like 'days till 9 Apr', while clipboard history lets you search and paste back the text, images, files and colours you've copied. Tinycast includes 35 window management commands for halves, thirds, nudges and moving between displays, plus layouts you can save. You can chat with Apple Intelligence, Claude, Codex, Grok, OpenCode or your own API key, and use Quick Actions to fix, rewrite, translate or summarize selected text in any app. It even runs Raycast extensions, uses under 100 MB of memory, and most features stay off until you turn them on. It's free and open source, with no account and no telemetry.

Key Features:

- App Launcher: find, open, pin, quit or restart apps in a few keystrokes

- Inline Calculator: math, units, currencies, time zones and date counts

- Clipboard History: search and paste back text, images, files and colours

- Window Management: 35 commands for halves, thirds, displays and saved layouts

- AI and Extensions: bring your own AI keys and run Raycast extensions

Tinycast is a lightweight, privacy-friendly Raycast alternative for the Mac, completely free and open source with no Pro tier.

apps.name: Chitra Studio
apps.tagline: Your AI media workstation.
apps.description:
Chitra Studio is a native Mac app for generating and managing AI images, videos, voices, music and sound effects using more than 60 models from Google, OpenAI, Black Forest Labs, ByteDance, Kling, Alibaba and others. Type a prompt, pick a model and see the exact cost in credits on the Generate button before you press it, and a generation that fails or is refused costs nothing. Compare runs the same prompt through several models side by side in a contact sheet where you can rate and keep the best results. Edit lets you draw a box around what should change while everything else stays pixel for pixel, Animate turns a still image into a clip, and Add Sound has a model watch your clip and create matching sound effects or music. You can also generate voices, music and sound effects, and every result lands in your library with its prompt, references and cost.

Key Features:

- 60+ AI Models: images, video, voices, music and sound effects in one app

- Price Before You Generate: see the credit cost before every run

- Compare Models: one prompt through several models side by side

- Edit and Animate: change only what you mark and turn stills into clips

- Organised Library: every result saved with its prompt, references and cost

Chitra Studio brings every major AI media model into one transparent Mac workspace, with a 14-day free trial including 50 credits, then $49 a year.

apps.name: talkflow
apps.tagline: Talk to your computer, for free, forever.
apps.description:
talkflow is a free, open-source voice dictation app and Wispr Flow alternative for Mac and PC. Hold the fn key, speak, and your words are typed wherever your cursor is, in any app, with no copying or pasting. Your words appear as you talk, and when you let go talkflow finishes the last words and fixes punctuation, turning casual speech into clean, punctuated text. Because most people talk much faster than they type, you can say the whole thought and get better prompts, emails and messages for the same effort. Speech recognition runs on your own processor using Whisper, so it works offline, audio is held in memory and never written to disk, and there's no sign-in or analytics. A dashboard in the menu bar shows your words, speed, streak and the typing time you've saved, and every line of code is public under the MIT License.

Key Features:

- Hold to Talk: hold fn, speak and text appears wherever your cursor is

- Works in Any App: types straight into whichever text field is active

- Clean Punctuation: spoken words turned into clean, punctuated text

- On-Device Whisper: runs locally and offline, with audio never saved

- Free and Open Source: MIT licensed with no word limits

talkflow is a fast, private way to write with your voice on Mac and PC, completely free with no word limit.

apps.name: SkillKeeper
apps.tagline: See what your AI coding setup actually runs.
apps.description:
SkillKeeper is a macOS menu bar app, and a Claude Code mod for Windows, Linux and Mac, that shows what your AI coding setup actually runs. It reads your local session logs from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Cursor and breaks usage down by skill, agent, tool, MCP server, command, memory file, hook and plugin, showing how often each one ran and how many tokens it spent over 5 hours, a day, a week or a month. Hooks show the time they add to your work, and MCP servers and plugins show what they cost. Agents display the skills they call, so you can see how your setup is really wired. SkillKeeper flags loops, clashing triggers, new skills and skills that never fire, and lets you edit a skill's description and triggers right from the menu bar without opening a file. Everything is read on your computer and never uploaded.

Key Features:

- Token Breakdown: every skill, agent, tool and MCP server ranked by tokens

- Hidden Costs: see the time hooks add and what MCP servers and plugins cost

- Setup Wiring: agents shown with the skills they call

- Attention Flags: loops, clashing triggers and skills that never fire

- Edit in Place: tweak skill descriptions and triggers from the menu bar

SkillKeeper gives you a clear view of where your AI coding tokens go, with a free plan for the weekly view and a one-time $19 license that unlocks everything.

apps.name: Virtual Diary
apps.tagline: Your diary, in your own hand.
apps.description:
Virtual Diary is a private paper diary app for iPad and Mac that gives you one page a day on warm ruled paper. On iPad you can write with Apple Pencil in black, blue or sepia ink with a proper eraser and undo, and on Mac you get the same paper page made for typing, with your choice of typeface and size. You can search every page you've ever written, handwriting included, with recognition done entirely on your device. On This Day shows what you wrote on the same date one, two or five years ago, and finished pages can be sealed like dried ink so they stay exactly as written. Your diary can be locked with Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode, and pages sync only through your own iCloud, with no account, no servers, no AI and no analytics.

Key Features:

- One Page a Day: a warm, ruled paper diary page for every day

- Handwriting or Typing: Apple Pencil ink on iPad, a typed page on Mac

- Search Everything: find any word, handwriting included, on device

- On This Day: look back at what you wrote in previous years

- Private by Design: Face ID lock, your own iCloud and no data collected

Virtual Diary brings the feel of a paper journal to iPad and Mac, with your first page free and a one-time $49 unlock ($69 for iPad and Mac together).

apps.name: CleanBrowse
apps.tagline: The internet, minus the worst of it.
apps.description:
CleanBrowse is a free macOS menu bar app that blocks adult content across your whole Mac, blurs explicit images in Safari and strips out ads and trackers, all from one menu bar icon. It filters every DNS query so more than 249,000 adult domains never load in any browser or app, locks search engines to SafeSearch and lets everything else pass through with no measurable slowdown, using the DNS provider of your choice. Its Safari extension uses on-device Core ML to check every image and video frame and blur anything explicit before it appears, from Google Images to social feeds and streaming sites. More than 120,000 ad and tracker rules stop ads, trackers, pop-unders and scam pages before they load. Work-site mode lets you pause blurring on tools like GitHub, Figma and Zoom while everything else stays protected. There are no accounts and no browsing data is ever collected.

Key Features:

- Adult-Site Blocking: 249,000+ domains blocked in every browser and app

- Explicit Image Blur: on-device AI blurs explicit images and video in Safari

- Ad and Tracker Blocking: 120,000+ rules for cleaner, faster pages

- Custom DNS Providers: choose your own DNS with SafeSearch enforced

- Work-Site Mode: pause blur on work tools while staying protected elsewhere

CleanBrowse offers private, system-wide protection from adult content, ads and trackers, completely free forever.

apps.name: Bayview
apps.tagline: Hassle-free window management for Mac.
apps.description:
Bayview is a grid-based window manager for Mac that lets you resize and move windows by dragging across a grid. Click the Bayview icon in the menu bar or press your shortcut, drag across the cells you want the window to fill and let go. The grid starts at 6 by 6 and can be made as fine as 12 by 12 for precise layouts. You can save any spot on the grid as a custom shortcut, such as the left half of the screen, and send the front window there without opening the grid at all. Pressing the same shortcut twice teleports a window to your next display, and keybinds let you grow, shrink or nudge windows one cell at a time so you can go completely mouseless. Every keybind is fully customizable, and Bayview works across multiple displays on macOS 13 or later.

Key Features:

- Grid Resizing: drag across cells to place and size any window

- Adjustable Grid: from 6 by 6 up to 12 by 12 for precise layouts

- Custom Shortcuts: save favourite positions and apply them instantly

- Teleport Windows: press a shortcut twice to move a window to the next screen

- Mouseless Control: keybinds to grow, shrink and nudge windows by a cell

Bayview gives you fast, precise control over your Mac windows, with a 6-hour free trial and a one-time $9.99 license for up to three devices.

apps.name: TuningMac
apps.tagline: Every sound on your Mac, perfectly tuned.
apps.description:
TuningMac is a system-wide equalizer and per-app volume mixer that lives in your Mac's menu bar. Give every app its own volume level, from Spotify and YouTube to Zoom, Slack and games, and shape the sound of everything you hear with nine presets like Bass Boost, Vocal and Rock or your own custom curves. A parametric mode offers up to 20 bands and six filter types for precise tuning, and you can import a measured correction for your exact headphones from AutoEQ in one click. TuningMac can play through several outputs at once, such as AirPods, speakers and your TV, each with its own volume and EQ, and remembers your setup when devices reconnect. Music can fade down automatically when a call starts, and you can switch AirPods noise cancelling and transparency without your phone. There are no drivers to install, no account and no tracking.

Key Features:

- Per-App Volume: set a separate volume level for every app

- System-Wide EQ: nine presets plus parametric EQ with up to 20 bands

- Headphone Correction: one-click AutoEQ profiles for 243 headphones

- Multi-Output Audio: play through up to 16 extra outputs in sync

- Auto Ducking and AirPods Control: music fades for calls, ANC from your Mac

TuningMac gives you full control over every sound on your Mac, with a 7-day free trial and a lifetime license for $5 for the first 100 buyers, then $14.

apps.name: Freshly Squeezed
apps.tagline: Batch resize, crop, convert, and optimize images on Mac.
apps.description:
Freshly Squeezed is a batch image processing app for Mac that turns folder after folder of product and web images into export-ready files, all locally. Drop in a folder of images and apply the same resize, crop, convert and optimize settings in one pass, or set up Drop Folders so every new image placed inside is processed automatically without even opening the app. It includes an interactive crop with social, web and print ratios, custom ratios and canvas extend with solid or transparent fill. You can fine-tune quality with a visual slider, export to JPEG, PNG, PNG-8, HEIC, WebP or AVIF, and keep or strip EXIF and GPS data. Presets save all your export settings, including crop placement, and sync across your Macs with iCloud. Built by an ecommerce tech lead for his own team, it's designed for designers, web developers, ecommerce managers and content creators.

Key Features:

- Batch Processing: resize, crop, convert and optimize whole folders at once

- Drop Folders: images are processed automatically as soon as they land

- Interactive Crop: social, web and print ratios plus canvas extend

- Format and Quality Control: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP and AVIF with EXIF stripping

- Presets with iCloud: save settings and sync them across your Macs

Freshly Squeezed automates repetitive image chores on the Mac, with a 7-day free trial and a one-time $6.99 lifetime license.

apps.name: Portlivo
apps.tagline: Every dev server. One click away.
apps.description:
Portlivo is a Mac menu bar app that shows every local dev server and port, from Vite, Next.js and Laravel to Docker, Postgres and Redis, along with the project each one belongs to. It scans every two seconds and turns a wall of lsof output into named, grouped live servers you can open, kill, restart, tail or share in one click. Each web server is health-checked and colour-coded by status with its response time, and live thumbnails show which localhost is which. When you hit an 'address already in use' error, Portlivo offers Kill Holder and Retry, and Stacks let you start a whole project's commands at once from a folder. You can share any server to your phone with a QR code or a public HTTPS link via Cloudflare or ngrok, use a command palette to control everything from the keyboard, and see which servers were started by Claude Code or Codex. It's a native SwiftUI app with no account and no analytics.

Key Features:

- Every Port at a Glance: named, grouped dev servers, databases and containers

- One-Click Actions: open, kill, restart, tail logs or share any server

- Port Conflict Fixes: Kill Holder and Retry when an address is in use

- Stacks: start a project's whole set of commands with one click

- Share and Agents: QR or public links, plus badges for Claude Code and Codex servers

Portlivo takes the pain out of juggling local dev servers, with a 7-day free trial and an early-bird one-time price of $8.99 (normally $19.99).

apps.name: Nijia
apps.tagline: See what's really using your Mac's storage.
apps.description:
Nijia is a storage analysis and cleanup app for Mac that helps you understand what's using your space before you delete anything. Space Analysis maps your whole drive in seconds so you can see where every gigabyte lives, including System Data, caches and build artifacts. Smart Cleanup clears only what can be rebuilt, matching derived files to the project or worktree that can recreate them, and nothing is deleted without your review. Dev Workspaces scans Git worktrees and AI agent sessions so you can see how much space each project and branch takes. Nijia also includes AI Desk Tidy to arrange your desktop without the busywork and System Watch for live disk, memory and load health. Every plan unlocks the full toolkit on up to two Macs, and you can try every feature free for seven days with no card required.

Key Features:

- Smart Cleanup: clear what can be rebuilt and keep what can't

- Space Analysis: map your whole drive and see where every gigabyte lives

- Dev Workspaces: scan worktrees and agent sessions for wasted space

- AI Desk Tidy: arrange your desktop automatically

- System Watch: live health for disk, memory and load

Nijia brings calm, review-first storage cleanup to the Mac, with a 7-day free trial and plans from $1.90 a month, $9.90 a year or $18.90 one-time at launch pricing.

apps.name: Bytebud
apps.tagline: Your Mac has feelings now.
apps.description:
Bytebud is a Mac menu bar app with a tiny creature that shows your Mac's health at a glance. Instead of a wall of graphs or a thousand processes in Activity Monitor, Bytebud folds memory pressure, heat, battery and disk space into one little face, and the worst signal wins. When something looks off, the creature turns Sick, Sweaty, Sleepy or Stuffed, and Bytebud points to the cause with a one-click fix, such as quitting the app hogging memory, closing one of the busiest apps when your Mac runs hot, switching on Low Power Mode or emptying the Trash when your disk is nearly full, always after you confirm. When everything is normal it's Happy, and you can pet it, watch it do tricks and build care streaks. Press R for a full report with a mood timeline, every vital over time and one row per app with Quit and Restart buttons. Bytebud is tiny and quiet, using around 0.17% idle CPU and 17 MB of memory, with no analytics or tracking.

Key Features:

- Menu Bar Creature: memory, heat, battery and disk folded into one face

- Five Moods: Sick, Sweaty, Sleepy, Stuffed and Happy show what's wrong

- One-Click Fixes: quit memory hogs, cool things down or free up disk space

- Full Report: mood timeline, vitals over time and per-app Quit and Restart

- Light and Private: tiny CPU and memory footprint, no tracking

Bytebud makes keeping an eye on your Mac's health fun and effortless, with an early-bird one-time price of $5.99 (then $9.99).

apps.name: Cortex
apps.tagline: The Activity Monitor for the AI era.
apps.description:
Cortex is a system monitor for macOS that turns a thousand processes into the sixty apps you actually run. Instead of a list of helpers, renderers and daemons, it counts each process under the app it belongs to, so a slow Mac has a name you recognise, and you can expand any app when you want the detail. Cortex keeps 30 days of history for every app and spots unusual behaviour, such as an app using several times its usual CPU for this hour. Its dashboard covers CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU, battery and thermals, and it goes further than Activity Monitor by showing what your Neural Engine and local AI models are doing. Developer and AI sections show projects, AI workloads and AI usage, and Cortex can tell you whether a local model will fit in your Mac's memory before you run it. Everything stays on your Mac, with no accounts, trackers or analytics.

Key Features:

- Apps, Not Processes: 1,000 processes grouped into the apps you run

- 30-Day History: see how every app has behaved over the past month

- Unusual Activity Alerts: flags apps running far above their normal baseline

- Neural Engine and AI: see what local models and AI workloads are doing

- Full System Dashboard: CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU, battery and thermals

Cortex is a modern, AI-aware Activity Monitor replacement for Apple Silicon Macs, available for a one-time $5 launch price.

apps.name: Timecard
apps.tagline: The Screen Time alternative for Mac.
apps.description:
Timecard is a screen time tracker and app blocker for Mac that shows exactly where your time goes and prints your day as a timecard every evening. It tracks time per app and splits your browser time into the real websites you visited, keeping your history forever instead of a few weeks.
